docs.text:
Window(content: Widget | RootFactory, width: WindowSizingLike = 'auto', height: WindowSizingLike = 'auto', *, title: str | None | ObservableBase[str | None] = None, chrome: OSChrome | CustomChrome | None = _UNSET, background: ColorSpec = SURFACE, overlay: Overlay | Callable[[], Overlay] | None = None, window_position: WindowPositionLike | None = None, resizable: bool = True, accepts_first_mouse: bool = True, menu: MenuBar | None = None, parent: Window | None = None, modal: bool = False, close_action: str | ObservableBase[str] = 'close')

One OS window: its widget tree, services, and lifecycle.

Construction builds a model only — no OS window, no mounted tree. :meth:open realizes it (and registers it with the running :class:~nuiitivet.runtime.app.App); :meth:close destroys it. One object is one window lifetime: a closed Window is finished, and showing the same content again means constructing a new one. State that must survive a window lives in app-layer Observables passed into the content.

Initialize the Window model. :meth:open realizes it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default content Widget | RootFactory

The root content. Accepts either a ready Widget instance or a root factory — a zero-argument callable returning the root Widget. Passing a factory is what enables hot reload under python -m nuiitivet.dev: the runner re-invokes it to rebuild the tree after a module reload. The resulting root may be a Navigator (used directly as the root Navigator) or any other Widget, in which case a default root Navigator is created implicitly.

required width WindowSizingLike

Window width specification.

'auto' height WindowSizingLike

Window height specification.

'auto' title str | None | ObservableBase[str | None]

OS window title. Accepts a plain string or an :class:~nuiitivet.observable.protocols.ObservableBase for dynamic updates. Pass None for no title.

None chrome OSChrome | CustomChrome | None

Window decoration. Pass an :class:OSChrome instance to use OS-managed decorations with an optional style variant, :class:CustomChrome for an app-drawn header, or None for a bare borderless window. Omitting this parameter (the default) is equivalent to OSChrome().

_UNSET background ColorSpec

Window background color.

SURFACE overlay Overlay | Callable[[], Overlay] | None

The window's overlay: an Overlay instance or a zero-argument factory returning one, under the same hot-reload rule as content. None gives the class default.

None window_position WindowPositionLike | None

Initial window position. Accepts a 9-point alignment string (e.g. "center", "top-right") or a :class:WindowPosition for offsets and screen selection.

None resizable bool

Whether the window can be resized.

True accepts_first_mouse bool

macOS only. When True (default), the click that activates this window while it is inactive is also delivered to the app, matching Windows/Linux and today's platform norm (Finder, Preview). Pass False to restore activate-only behavior for windows where an accidental first click could commit something. No effect on other platforms — they always deliver the click.

True menu MenuBar | None

The menu bar model (:class:~nuiitivet.menubar.MenuBar), or None for no menu bar. Replace it wholesale via window.menu = ....

None parent Window | None

The parent window, or None for a top-level window. A child stacks with its parent and closes when it closes.

None modal bool

Whether this window blocks input to its parent chain while open (framework modal). Requires parent.

False close_action str | ObservableBase[str]

What the OS close button does: "close" (default) destroys the window; "hide" parks it — :meth:hide — so a tray-resident app can be summoned back. Accepts an Observable so the choice can follow live state; the resident recipe binds it to TrayIcon.installed (hide only while the tray is actually showing). Programmatic :meth:close is unaffected.

'close' Source code in src/nuiitivet/runtime/window.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    content: "Widget | RootFactory",
    width: WindowSizingLike = "auto",
    height: WindowSizingLike = "auto",
    *,
    title: "str | None | ObservableBase[str | None]" = None,
    chrome: "OSChrome | CustomChrome | None" = _UNSET,  # type: ignore[assignment]
    background: ColorSpec = PlainColorRole.SURFACE,
    overlay: "Overlay | Callable[[], Overlay] | None" = None,
    window_position: WindowPositionLike | None = None,
    resizable: bool = True,
    accepts_first_mouse: bool = True,
    menu: "MenuBar | None" = None,
    parent: "Window | None" = None,
    modal: bool = False,
    close_action: "str | ObservableBase[str]" = "close",
):
    """Initialize the Window model. :meth:`open` realizes it.

    Args:
        content: The root content. Accepts either a ready ``Widget``
            instance or a **root factory** — a zero-argument callable
            returning the root ``Widget``. Passing a factory is what
            enables hot reload under ``python -m nuiitivet.dev``: the
            runner re-invokes it to rebuild the tree after a module
            reload. The resulting root may be a ``Navigator`` (used
            directly as the root Navigator) or any other ``Widget``, in
            which case a default root ``Navigator`` is created implicitly.
        width: Window width specification.
        height: Window height specification.
        title: OS window title. Accepts a plain string or an
            :class:`~nuiitivet.observable.protocols.ObservableBase` for
            dynamic updates. Pass ``None`` for no title.
        chrome: Window decoration. Pass an :class:`OSChrome` instance to
            use OS-managed decorations with an optional style variant,
            :class:`CustomChrome` for an app-drawn header, or ``None``
            for a bare borderless window. Omitting this parameter (the
            default) is equivalent to ``OSChrome()``.
        background: Window background color.
        overlay: The window's overlay: an ``Overlay`` instance or a
            zero-argument factory returning one, under the same hot-reload
            rule as ``content``. ``None`` gives the class default.
        window_position: Initial window position. Accepts a 9-point
            alignment string (e.g. ``"center"``, ``"top-right"``) or a
            :class:`WindowPosition` for offsets and screen selection.
        resizable: Whether the window can be resized.
        accepts_first_mouse: macOS only. When ``True`` (default), the
            click that activates this window while it is inactive is
            also delivered to the app, matching Windows/Linux and
            today's platform norm (Finder, Preview). Pass ``False`` to
            restore activate-only behavior for windows where an
            accidental first click could commit something. No effect
            on other platforms — they always deliver the click.
        menu: The menu bar model (:class:`~nuiitivet.menubar.MenuBar`),
            or ``None`` for no menu bar. Replace it wholesale via
            ``window.menu = ...``.
        parent: The parent window, or ``None`` for a top-level window.
            A child stacks with its parent and closes when it closes.
        modal: Whether this window blocks input to its parent chain
            while open (framework modal). Requires ``parent``.
        close_action: What the OS close button does: ``"close"`` (default)
            destroys the window; ``"hide"`` parks it — :meth:`hide` —
            so a tray-resident app can be summoned back. Accepts an
            Observable so the choice can follow live state; the resident
            recipe binds it to ``TrayIcon.installed`` (hide only while
            the tray is actually showing). Programmatic :meth:`close`
            is unaffected.
    """
    # Normalize ``content`` to a root factory. A Widget instance is wrapped
    # in a factory that always returns that same instance (so hot reload is
    # a no-op for it); a callable is stored as-is. ``self._root_factory`` is
    # the single source of truth the reload path re-invokes.
    if callable(content) and not isinstance(content, Widget):
        self._root_factory: RootFactory = content
        content_inert = False
    elif isinstance(content, Widget):
        instance = content
        self._root_factory = lambda: instance
        # The wrapping lambda can never be re-fetched from a reloaded
        # module, so every rebuild returns this same object: hot reload
        # can never change this window's tree.
        content_inert = True
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            "'content' must be a Widget instance or a callable returning a Widget."
        )

    from nuiitivet.overlay import Overlay

    # ``overlay`` follows the ``content`` rule; the reload path re-invokes the factory.
    overlay_inert = False
    if overlay is None:
        self._overlay_factory: Callable[[], "Overlay"] = self._build_default_overlay
    elif isinstance(overlay, Overlay):
        overlay_instance = overlay
        self._overlay_factory = lambda: overlay_instance
        overlay_inert = True
    elif callable(overlay):
        self._overlay_factory = overlay
    else:
        raise TypeError("'overlay' must be an Overlay instance or a callable returning an Overlay.")
    self._hot_reload_inert = content_inert or overlay_inert

    if parent is not None and not isinstance(parent, Window):
        raise TypeError("'parent' must be a Window instance or None.")
    if modal and parent is None:
        raise ValueError("modal=True requires a parent window.")
    self._parent: "Window | None" = parent
    self._modal = bool(modal)

    # Stable per-process identity, used by tooling (the dev bridge's
    # window selector) and useful in logs. Never reused within a process.
    self.id: int = next(_window_ids)

    # Warn once, at the moment the app shape can still be fixed. Only under
    # the dev runner: in production there is no hot reload to be inert for.
    if content_inert and _under_dev_session():
        root_name = type(content).__name__
        logger.warning(
            "Window id=%d content is a widget instance (%s); hot reload "
            "cannot apply edits to this window. Pass a factory instead: "
            "Window(content=%s) or Window(content=lambda: %s(...)).",
            self.id,
            root_name,
            root_name,
            root_name,
        )
    if overlay_inert and _under_dev_session():
        overlay_name = type(overlay).__name__
        logger.warning(
            "Window id=%d overlay is an instance (%s); hot reload keeps it "
            "and its intents table. Pass a factory instead: "
            "Window(overlay=lambda: %s(...)).",
            self.id,
            overlay_name,
            overlay_name,
        )

    if not isinstance(close_action, ObservableBase) and close_action not in ("close", "hide"):
        raise ValueError('close_action must be "close", "hide", or an Observable of one.')
    self._close_action: "str | ObservableBase[str]" = close_action

    # Lifecycle: created -> open -> closed, one way. Visibility is
    # orthogonal: a hidden window is still open (and still counts for the
    # App's exit policy).
    self._app_ref: Any = None
    self._lifecycle_state: str = "created"
    self._is_open_obs: Observable[bool] = Observable(False)
    self._visible_obs: Observable[bool] = Observable(True)
    self._closed_event: Any = None
    self._os_active = False
    # Per-window IME geometry (cursor rect, window location). Written by
    # this window's focused text field and its backend window, read by the
    # platform IME hook installed on this OS window. See design doc 8.6.
    self._ime = IMEManager()

    self._width_spec: WindowSizingLike = width
    self._height_spec: WindowSizingLike = height

    self.chrome: OSChrome | CustomChrome | None = OSChrome() if chrome is _UNSET else chrome
    # Reset the drag-area reference (class default is None); a CustomChrome
    # rebuilds it in :meth:`_wrap_with_chrome_and_scope`.
    self._window_drag_area = None

    # Menu bar: the controller owns the registered model and the slots
    # rendering it. The default slot is inserted below the chrome (see
    # :meth:`_wrap_with_chrome_and_scope`) only when a menu was registered
    # at construction; a MenuBarArea in the tree takes over regardless.
    from nuiitivet.menubar.controller import MenuBarController

    self._menubar_controller: MenuBarController = MenuBarController(self, menu)

    # Provisional window size. An ``auto`` dimension is resolved at the end
    # of :meth:`open`, once the tree is mounted and can be measured against
    # the real theme; until then ``on_mount`` code that reads window.width /
    # window.height must still see a number rather than an AttributeError.
    self.width = self._resolve_window_sizing(width, preferred=0, fallback=640)
    self.height = self._resolve_window_sizing(height, preferred=0, fallback=480)
    self.window_position = None if window_position is None else parse_window_position(window_position)
    self.resizable = resizable
    self.accepts_first_mouse = bool(accepts_first_mouse)

    self._title_value: str | None | ObservableBase[str | None] = title
    self._title_disposable: Optional[Disposable] = None

    self._scale = 1.0
    self._dirty = False
    # Content dirtiness is distinct from ``_dirty``: ``_dirty`` means "a frame
    # was requested", while ``_paint_dirty`` means "the widget tree changed and
    # must be re-painted". A surface-loss redraw (window show/activate) or a
    # dev overlay change requests a frame without changing content, letting
    # the renderer reuse the tree it last painted instead of walking it again.
    self._paint_dirty = True
    # The raster path's last painted tree, without overlays; the GPU path
    # keeps its own in ``draw_gpu_frame``.
    self._content_image: Any = None
    self._window = None
    self._event_loop: Any = None
    self._last_hover_target = None
    self._focused_target: Optional[InteractionHostMixin] = None
    self._focused_node: Optional[FocusNode] = None
    # Open blocking overlay entries, innermost last, each paired with the node
    # that held focus when it opened. A modal takes focus with it and hands it
    # back on close; the invoker cannot be looked up from the tree afterwards,
    # because by then the dialog is detached. See :meth:`_sync_overlay_focus_trap`.
    self._overlay_focus_trap: list[Tuple[Widget, Optional[FocusNode]]] = []
    # How the user is driving the app right now. A widget that takes focus on
    # its own (a menu focusing its first item when it opens) inherits it, so a
    # mouse-opened menu does not come up wearing a keyboard focus ring.
    self._last_input_source: FocusSource = FocusSource.KEYBOARD
    self._modifier_keys: int = 0
    # Dev-only observer for the interaction journal. The dev runner
    # attaches an ``InteractionRecorder`` here so the human's coarse UI
    # actions can be recorded for an agent to pull; ``None`` -- and zero
    # overhead -- in production.
    self._interaction_recorder: Optional[Any] = None
    # Dev-only mark mode. The dev runner attaches a
    # ``CommentMode`` here so the human can point at a widget for an agent
    # to read; ``None`` -- and zero overhead -- in production.
    self._comment_mode: Optional[Any] = None
    # Dev-only source jump. The dev runner attaches a ``SourceJump`` here so
    # a chorded click opens the code that built a widget; ``None`` in
    # production.
    self._source_jump: Optional[Any] = None
    # Dev-only layout edit mode. The dev runner attaches a ``LayoutEditMode`` here so
    # a corner drag rewrites the size in the source; ``None`` in production.
    self._layout_edit_mode: Optional[Any] = None
    # Last known pointer position / held buttons (screen coords), used to
    # synthesize the pointer event delivered on a modifier-key mask change.
    self._last_pointer_pos: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None
    self._last_pointer_buttons: int = 0
    self._pointer_capture_manager = PointerCaptureManager()
    self._pointer_capture_manager.set_cancel_callback(self._handle_pointer_cancel)
    self._primary_pointer_id = 1
    self._background_value: ColorSpec = background
    # Resolved lazily (and re-resolved on theme change): resolution needs
    # the App's theme, which this Window meets at :meth:`open`.
    self._background_color: Any = None
    self._last_layout_size: Optional[tuple[int, int]] = None
    self._saved_window_rect: Optional[tuple[int, int, int, int]] = None

    def _env_flag(name: str, default: bool = False) -> bool:
        raw = os.environ.get(name)
        if raw is None:
            return default
        value = str(raw).strip().lower()
        if value in ("", "0", "false", "no", "off", "disable", "disabled"):
            return False
        if value in ("1", "true", "yes", "on", "enable", "enabled"):
            return True
        return True

    self._debug_invalidate = _env_flag("NUIITIVET_DEBUG_INVALIDATE", default=False)
    self._invalidate_report_every_s = float(os.environ.get("NUIITIVET_DEBUG_INVALIDATE_EVERY", "1.0"))
    self._invalidate_report_every_s = max(0.1, self._invalidate_report_every_s)

@staticmethod
def of(context: Widget) -> "Window":
    """Return the Window whose tree contains ``context``.

    The returned object is the same ``Window`` the opener holds — there is
    no proxy type. A ViewModel should receive it typed as
    :class:`~nuiitivet.runtime.protocols.WindowProtocol`. Valid from
    ``on_mount``, not from ``__init__``, like every ``.of()`` lookup.

    Args:
        context: The widget context.

    Returns:
        The owning Window.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If called before ``context`` is mounted (typically
            from ``__init__``), or if the widget is not attached to a
            Window.
    """
    scope = find_provider(context, WindowScope)
    window = scope.window if scope is not None else None
    if window is None:
        raise_if_premature_lookup("Window.of", context)
        raise RuntimeError("WindowScope not found. Is the widget attached to a Window?")
    return window

def can_handle_back_event(self) -> bool:
    """Return True if a back action would be handled.

    This is a non-mutating check used by backends to decide whether to
    consume the OS/back key or let default handlers run (e.g. ESC-to-exit).
    """

    overlay = self._overlay
    if overlay is not None:
        try:
            if overlay.has_entries():
                return True
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "app_overlay_has_entries_exc", "overlay.has_entries() failed")

    navigator = self._navigator
    if navigator is not None:
        try:
            return bool(navigator.can_pop())
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "app_navigator_can_pop_exc", "navigator.can_pop() failed")
            return False

    return False

Handle a user back action (e.g. Esc).

Priority: - Overlay: close topmost entry if any - Navigator: pop one route if possible

A back action never reaches past a blocking layer. If the overlay had nothing left to close but is still painting one -- a dialog already dismissed and animating out is the case that reaches here -- the event stops, rather than popping the screen the user can still see behind it. This is the keyboard half of what Overlay.hit_test does for the pointer; a pass-through layer (toast, banner) blocks neither.

Source code in src/nuiitivet/runtime/window.py 
async def handle_back_event(self) -> bool:
    """Handle a user back action (e.g. Esc).

    Priority:
    - Overlay: close topmost entry if any
    - Navigator: pop one route if possible

    A back action never reaches past a blocking layer. If the overlay had
    nothing left to close but is still painting one -- a dialog already
    dismissed and animating out is the case that reaches here -- the event
    stops, rather than popping the screen the user can still see behind it.
    This is the keyboard half of what ``Overlay.hit_test`` does for the
    pointer; a pass-through layer (toast, banner) blocks neither.
    """

    overlay = self._overlay
    if overlay is not None:
        try:
            has_entries = bool(overlay.has_entries())
            if has_entries:
                handled = bool(await overlay.async_request_close_topmost())
                if handled:
                    return True
                if overlay.occluding_content_widget() is not None:
                    return True
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "app_overlay_close_topmost_exc", "overlay.close_topmost() failed")

    navigator = self._navigator
    if navigator is not None:
        try:
            request_back = getattr(navigator, "request_back", None)
            if callable(request_back):
                handled = bool(await request_back())
                return handled
            if navigator.can_pop():
                navigator.pop()
                return True
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "app_navigator_back_exc", "Navigator back handling failed")
    return False

def open(self) -> "Window":
    """Realize the window: build and mount the tree, register with the App.

    The OS window itself is created by the running backend — immediately
    when the loop is already running, or when ``app.run()`` starts for
    windows opened before it.

    Returns:
        ``self``, for chaining.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the window is already open, is already closed
            (one object is one window lifetime), no App exists yet, or
            the parent window is not open.
    """
    if self._lifecycle_state == "open":
        raise RuntimeError("Window is already open.")
    if self._lifecycle_state == "closed":
        raise RuntimeError(
            "A closed Window is finished; construct a new Window to show its content again."
        )
    app = self._app_ref() if self._app_ref is not None else None
    if app is None:
        from nuiitivet.runtime.app import current_app

        app = current_app()
        if app is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Window.open() requires an App; construct the App first.")
        self._app_ref = weakref.ref(app)
    if self._parent is not None and self._parent._lifecycle_state != "open":
        raise RuntimeError("Window.open(): the parent window is not open.")

    content_root = self._root_factory()
    if not isinstance(content_root, Widget):
        raise TypeError("root factory must return a Widget instance.")

    from nuiitivet.navigation import Navigator

    if isinstance(content_root, Navigator):
        navigator = content_root
    else:
        navigator = self._build_default_navigator(content_root)

    built = self._build_root_navigation_stack(
        navigator=navigator,
        overlay_factory=self._overlay_factory,
    )
    # Nothing to unmount on the initial path, so adopt straight away; the
    # reload path defers this to :meth:`_commit_content_root`.
    self._navigator = built.navigator
    self._overlay = built.overlay

    # Apply the chrome decoration and scope wrapping. This must precede the
    # auto-size measurement below: the AppScope installed here is what
    # ``Theme.of`` resolves against, so a tree measured before it exists is
    # measured against the default theme.
    self.root = self._wrap_with_chrome_and_scope(built.widget)

    self._update_background_color()
    self._subscribe_title_updates()

    self._lifecycle_state = "open"
    self._is_open_obs.value = True

    # Mounting comes after every attribute a lifecycle hook might touch is
    # initialized (see ``__init__``): ``mount()`` runs on_mount for the
    # whole tree, and that user code can call straight back into the Window.
    try:
        self.root.mount(self)
    except Exception:
        exception_once(logger, "window_open_root_mount_exc", "root.mount(self) raised during Window.open()")

    width_sizing = parse_window_sizing(self._width_spec)
    height_sizing = parse_window_sizing(self._height_spec)
    if width_sizing.kind == "auto" or height_sizing.kind == "auto":
        self._apply_auto_window_size(
            width=self._width_spec,
            height=self._height_spec,
            target=built.initial_route_widget,
            chrome=self.chrome,
        )

    app._register_window(self)
    self._notify_visibility_changed()
    return self

Source code in src/nuiitivet/runtime/window.py 
def close(self) -> None:
    """Destroy the window: unmount the tree and close the OS window.

    Closing is one-way — the object is finished afterwards. Children close
    first, transitively. Closing a window that is not open is a no-op.
    """
    if self._lifecycle_state != "open":
        return
    app = self._app_ref() if self._app_ref is not None else None

    if app is not None:
        for child in [w for w in app.windows if w.parent is self]:
            try:
                child.close()
            except Exception:
                exception_once(logger, "window_close_child_exc", "Closing a child window raised")

    self._lifecycle_state = "closed"
    self._is_open_obs.value = False

    self._unsubscribe_title_updates()

    try:
        root = getattr(self, "root", None)
        if root is not None:
            root.unmount()
    except Exception:
        exception_once(logger, "window_close_root_unmount_exc", "root.unmount raised")

    self._reset_interaction_state()

    os_window = self._window
    self._window = None
    self._event_loop = None
    if os_window is not None:
        try:
            os_window.close()
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "window_close_os_window_exc", "Backend window close raised")

    event = self._closed_event
    if event is not None:
        try:
            event.set()
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "window_closed_event_set_exc", "closed event set raised")

    if app is not None:
        app._unregister_window(self)
    # After unregistration, so the menu bar coordinator re-resolves
    # against the open set without this window.
    self._menubar_controller.window_closed()
    self._notify_visibility_changed()

def hide(self) -> None:
    """Hide the window, keeping the object and its widget tree alive.

    The counterpart of :meth:`show` — the pair a tray-resident app parks
    and summons its window with. Before the backend realizes the OS
    window this just records the desired state (so a window can start
    hidden); hiding a window that is not open is a no-op.
    """
    if self._lifecycle_state != "open" or not self._visible_obs.value:
        return
    self._visible_obs.value = False
    window = self._window
    if window is not None:
        try:
            window.set_visible(False)
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "window_hide_exc", "Window.hide failed")
    self._notify_visibility_changed()

def show(self) -> None:
    """Make the window visible and bring it to the front, focused.

    Also the "summon" action for an already-visible window: it raises
    and refocuses. Showing a window that is not open is a no-op (a
    closed Window is finished — construct a new one).
    """
    if self._lifecycle_state != "open":
        return
    was_hidden = not self._visible_obs.value
    self._visible_obs.value = True
    if was_hidden:
        # Before the OS window reappears, so a dock_visibility="auto"
        # tray restores the regular activation policy first.
        self._notify_visibility_changed()
    window = self._window
    if window is not None:
        try:
            window.set_visible(True)
            window.activate()
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "window_show_exc", "Window.show failed")
        if was_hidden:
            self.invalidate(immediate=True)

def invalidate(self, immediate: bool = False, content: bool = True):
    """Request that the next frame be redrawn.

    This sets an internal dirty flag which the render loop checks to
    decide whether to re-render the UI.

    Args:
        immediate: If True and running in pyglet, bypass FPS throttle for next draw
        content: If True (default), mark the widget tree as changed so the next
            frame re-paints it. Pass False when the tree is unchanged and only
            what lies over it needs the frame: a surface-loss redraw (window
            show/activate) or a dev overlay. The renderer then reuses the tree
            it last painted instead of walking it again.
    """
    self._dirty = True
    if content:
        self._paint_dirty = True
    self._debug_record_invalidate()
    loop = self._event_loop
    if loop is not None:
        try:
            loop.request_draw(immediate=immediate)
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "app_request_draw_exc", "Event loop request_draw raised")

def request_focus(self, node: Optional[FocusNode], source: FocusSource = FocusSource.KEYBOARD) -> None:
    """Set focus to the given FocusNode. Pass ``None`` to clear focus."""
    if self._focused_node is node:
        # Same node, possibly a different source: a pointer press on the widget
        # that Tab already focused still has to hide its focus ring.
        if node is not None:
            node.notify_focus_source(source)
        return

    # Blur previous node
    if self._focused_node:
        self._focused_node._set_focused(False)

    # Focus new node
    self._focused_node = node
    if node:
        node._set_focused(True, source)
        # Also update legacy target if the node belongs to a widget
        if node.region:
            self._focused_target = node.region
    else:
        self._focused_target = None

def center(self) -> None:
    """Center the window on its screen."""
    window = self._window

    try:

        if screen:

def maximize(self) -> None:
    """Maximize the window."""
    window = self._window
    if window is None:
        return
    try:
        # Save current window rect before maximizing
        try:
            wx, wy = window.get_location()
            ww, wh = window.width, window.height
            self._saved_window_rect = (wx, wy, ww, wh)
        except Exception:
            self._saved_window_rect = None

        if sys.platform == "darwin":
            try:
                import ctypes
                from pyglet.libs.darwin import cocoapy
                from pyglet.libs.darwin.cocoapy import cocoatypes

                ns_window = window._nswindow
                screen = ns_window.screen()
                # visibleFrame returns NSRect
                visible_frame = cocoapy.send_message(screen, "visibleFrame", restype=cocoatypes.NSRect)
                # setFrame:display:
                # void setFrame:(NSRect)frameRect display:(BOOL)flag
                cocoapy.send_message(
                    ns_window,
                    "setFrame:display:",
                    visible_frame,
                    True,
                    argtypes=[cocoatypes.NSRect, ctypes.c_bool],
                )
            except Exception:
                # Fallback if something goes wrong (e.g. older pyglet)
                window.maximize()
        else:
            window.maximize()
    except Exception:
        exception_once(logger, "window_maximize_exc", "Window.maximize failed")

def restore(self) -> None:
    """Restore the window from maximized/minimized/full-screen state."""
    window = self._window
    if window is None:
        return
    try:
        if window.fullscreen:
            window.set_fullscreen(False)
            return

        try:
            if sys.platform == "win32":
                import ctypes

                SW_RESTORE = 9
                hwnd = getattr(window, "_hwnd", None)
                if hwnd:
                    ctypes.windll.user32.ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_RESTORE)
        except Exception:
            exception_once(logger, "window_restore_win32_exc", "Windows restore fallback failed")

        # Try to activate (restore from minimize on some platforms)
        if hasattr(window, "activate"):
            window.activate()

        # Restore from maximize if we have saved state
        if self._saved_window_rect is not None:
            try:
                rx, ry, rw, rh = self._saved_window_rect
                window.set_location(rx, ry)
                window.set_size(rw, rh)
                self._saved_window_rect = None
            except Exception:
                exception_once(logger, "window_restore_rect_exc", "Failed to restore window rect")

        # Note: Pyglet doesn't have a direct 'unmaximize' or 'restore' from maximize
        # that is consistent across platforms.
    except Exception:
        exception_once(logger, "window_restore_exc", "Window.restore failed")

def allow(pattern: Union[str, Pattern[str]]) -> InputFilter:
    """Keep only the characters that match ``pattern``, dropping the rest.

    The pattern is matched against one character at a time, so

matching(pattern: Union[str, Pattern[str]]) -> InputFilter

Reject an edit unless the resulting text matches pattern in full.

Unlike :func:allow, which filters character by character and always accepts something, this rejects the keystroke outright when the result would not match -- the rule it enforces is about the text as a whole, so there is no partial result to keep. It is what expresses "at most one decimal point"::

The pattern must accept every string the user has to be able to pass through on the way to a finished value, including "" if the field is to be clearable.

def matching(pattern: Union[str, Pattern[str]]) -> InputFilter:
    """Reject an edit unless the resulting text matches ``pattern`` in full.

    Unlike :func:`allow`, which filters character by character and always
    accepts something, this rejects the keystroke outright when the result
    would not match -- the rule it enforces is about the text as a whole, so
    there is no partial result to keep. It is what expresses "at most one
    decimal point"::

        input_filter=matching(r"[0-9]*\\.?[0-9]*")

    The pattern must accept every string the user has to be able to pass
    through on the way to a finished value, including ``""`` if the field is to
    be clearable.
    """
    return _MatchingFilter(_compile(pattern))

docs.text:
server(fn: Callable[P, R]) -> Callable[P, Coroutine[Any, Any, R]]

Mark a function as one that runs on the server when the app is on the web.

The app awaits it the same way on both targets::

@nv.server
def load_orders(user_id: int) -> list[Order]: ...

orders = await load_orders(42)

On the desktop it runs on a worker thread. Either way it shares nothing with its caller: arguments and the result are copied, and may only be of the types that survive a connection -- None, bool, int, float, str, bytes, datetime, date, an Enum, a dataclass of these, list[T], tuple[T, ...], dict[str, T] and T | None. An Enum or dataclass in the signature is defined in a module the page gets, not in a server-only one.

Two parameter types are not data. WriteOnlyObservable[T] receives an Observable of the caller for the function to report progress into. CancelToken, declared with a default and never passed by the caller, is set when the awaiting task is cancelled.

An exception reaches the caller: a built-in one as itself, any other as :class:RemoteError.

The function's module reaches the browser like any other, and the function's body never runs there. A module that must stay on the server calls :func:~nuiitivet.remote.scope.server_only.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fn Callable[P, R]

A plain def at the top level of a module in the app's directory, with every parameter and the return type annotated.

required

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If fn breaks one of these rules.

Source code in src/nuiitivet/remote/function.py 
def server(fn: Callable[P, R]) -> Callable[P, Coroutine[Any, Any, R]]:
    """Mark a function as one that runs on the server when the app is on the web.

    The app awaits it the same way on both targets::

        @nv.server
        def load_orders(user_id: int) -> list[Order]: ...

        orders = await load_orders(42)

    On the desktop it runs on a worker thread. Either way it shares nothing
    with its caller: arguments and the result are copied, and may only be of
    the types that survive a connection -- ``None``, ``bool``, ``int``,
    ``float``, ``str``, ``bytes``, ``datetime``, ``date``, an ``Enum``, a
    dataclass of these, ``list[T]``, ``tuple[T, ...]``, ``dict[str, T]`` and
    ``T | None``. An ``Enum`` or dataclass in the signature is defined in a
    module the page gets, not in a server-only one.

    Two parameter types are not data. ``WriteOnlyObservable[T]`` receives an
    ``Observable`` of the caller for the function to report progress into.
    ``CancelToken``, declared with a default and never passed by the caller,
    is set when the awaiting task is cancelled.

    An exception reaches the caller: a built-in one as itself, any other as
    :class:`RemoteError`.

    The function's module reaches the browser like any other, and the
    function's body never runs there. A module that must stay on the server
    calls :func:`~nuiitivet.remote.scope.server_only`.

    Args:
        fn: A plain ``def`` at the top level of a module in the app's
            directory, with every parameter and the return type annotated.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If *fn* breaks one of these rules.
    """
    return register(ServerFunction(fn))

server_only() -> None

Declare that the calling module never leaves the server.

Call it at the top of a module. In a package's __init__.py it covers every module and file of the package. The web build leaves what is declared out of the page; a @server function in it is answered by a stub with its signature. Database addresses, keys, and an import the browser cannot do belong here. A @worker function cannot.

Raises:

Type Description RuntimeError

If the module is loaded in a browser.

Source code in src/nuiitivet/remote/scope.py 
def server_only() -> None:
    """Declare that the calling module never leaves the server.

    Call it at the top of a module. In a package's ``__init__.py`` it covers
    every module and file of the package. The web build leaves what is
    declared out of the page; a ``@server`` function in it is answered by a
    stub with its signature. Database addresses, keys, and an import the
    browser cannot do belong here. A ``@worker`` function cannot.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the module is loaded in a browser.
    """
    name = sys._getframe(1).f_globals["__name__"]
    if is_web():
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} is server-only and was loaded in the browser")
    _server_only.add(name)

docs.title: on_size_changed
docs.text:
on_size_changed(callback: SizeCallback) -> OnSizeChangedModifier

Return a modifier that calls callback with the widget's measured size.

The callback receives a :class:Size - the widget's own (width, height) after layout, excluding its position. Use it to feed a size into imperative state: a ViewModel, or a plain Observable a child widget binds to::

class ResponsiveScaffold(ComposableWidget):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.expanded = Observable(False)

    def _on_size(self, size: Size) -> None:
        self.expanded.value = size.width >= 700

    def build(self) -> Widget:
        rail = NavigationRail(..., expanded=self.expanded)
        return Row([rail, card], ...).modifier(on_size_changed(self._on_size))

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default callback SizeCallback

A callable taking a :class:Size, sync or async. An async callback is scheduled as a task. Exceptions are logged and contained.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description An OnSizeChangedModifier

class:OnSizeChangedModifier to apply via widget.modifier(...).

Note

Fires once with the first measurement, so the callback alone is enough to seed the state it drives. After that it fires only when the measured size actually changed; a widget that is re-laid-out at the same size, or merely moved, is silent.

Note

Dispatched between frames, never during layout, so the callback may safely do anything - push a route, write an Observable, replace children - and its effect lands on the frame after the measurement.

That includes the first call, which therefore arrives after the first paint. Give an Observable the value you expect at the initial size and the first report writes the same value, which de-dupes: no visible transition. Seed it differently and the widget animates once on startup.

Warning

Avoid making the callback change the measured widget's own size: that feeds back into the next measurement and can oscillate. The structurally safe pattern is to measure a widget whose size the parent imposes (Sizing.weight(...) / "wt") and let the callback change only what is inside it.

Source code in src/nuiitivet/modifiers/size_changed.py 
def on_size_changed(callback: SizeCallback) -> OnSizeChangedModifier:
    """Return a modifier that calls *callback* with the widget's measured size.

    The callback receives a :class:`Size` - the widget's own ``(width, height)``
    after layout, excluding its position. Use it to feed a size into imperative
    state: a ViewModel, or a plain ``Observable`` a child widget binds to::

        class ResponsiveScaffold(ComposableWidget):
            def __init__(self) -> None:
                super().__init__()
                self.expanded = Observable(False)

            def _on_size(self, size: Size) -> None:
                self.expanded.value = size.width >= 700

            def build(self) -> Widget:
                rail = NavigationRail(..., expanded=self.expanded)
                return Row([rail, card], ...).modifier(on_size_changed(self._on_size))

    Args:
        callback: A callable taking a :class:`Size`, sync or async. An async
            callback is scheduled as a task. Exceptions are logged and contained.

    Returns:
        An :class:`OnSizeChangedModifier` to apply via ``widget.modifier(...)``.

    Note:
        **Fires once with the first measurement**, so the callback alone is
        enough to seed the state it drives. After that it fires only when the
        measured size actually changed; a widget that is re-laid-out at the same
        size, or merely moved, is silent.

    Note:
        **Dispatched between frames, never during layout**, so the callback may
        safely do anything - push a route, write an Observable, replace
        children - and its effect lands on the frame after the measurement.

        That includes the first call, which therefore arrives *after* the first
        paint. Give an Observable the value you expect at the initial size and
        the first report writes the same value, which de-dupes: no visible
        transition. Seed it differently and the widget animates once on startup.

    Warning:
        Avoid making the callback change the measured widget's *own* size: that
        feeds back into the next measurement and can oscillate. The structurally
        safe pattern is to measure a widget whose size the parent imposes
        (``Sizing.weight(...)`` / ``"wt"``) and let the callback change only what
        is *inside* it.
    """
    return OnSizeChangedModifier(callback=callback)

Hard line breaks (\n) and soft wrapping both count toward this limit. - overflow: What to do when text exceeds the layout box: "visible" (draw beyond bounds), "clip" (cut at the edge), or "ellipsis" (truncate the last visible line with …). - truncation: Where the ellipsis is placed — "tail", "head" or "middle". Only meaningful when overflow="ellipsis". - soft_wrap: Whether text wraps at soft line breaks when the width is bounded. Hard breaks (\n) always break regardless of this flag.

def __init__(
    self,
    label: Union[str, ReadOnlyObservableProtocol[Any]],
    style: Optional[TextStyleProtocol] = None,
    width: SizingLike = None,
    height: SizingLike = None,
    padding: Union[int, Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int, int, int]] = 0,
    *,
    type_scale: Optional[TypeScaleToken] = None,
    alignment: Literal["start", "center", "end"] = "start",
    max_lines: Optional[int] = None,
    overflow: Literal["visible", "clip", "ellipsis"] = "visible",
    truncation: Literal["tail", "head", "middle"] = "tail",
    soft_wrap: bool = True,
    key: Optional[str] = None,
):
    super().__init__(width=width, height=height, padding=padding, key=key)
    self.label = label

    # Use provided style or None (resolved via property)
    self._style = style

    # Typography comes from the type-scale token (not the style).
    self._type_scale = type_scale

    # Alignment is a layout/flow concern and lives on the widget.
    self._alignment: str = alignment if alignment in ("start", "center", "end") else "start"

    # Overflow / wrapping behavior lives on the widget, not the style.
    self._max_lines = self._normalize_max_lines(max_lines)
    self._overflow: str = overflow if overflow in ("visible", "clip", "ellipsis") else "visible"
    self._truncation: str = truncation if truncation in ("tail", "head", "middle") else "tail"
    self._soft_wrap: bool = bool(soft_wrap)

    # instance attribute tracking a Disposable returned by subscribe
    self._label_unsub = None

    self._paint_cache = None
    self._look: ThemeKept[_Look] = ThemeKept()

def preferred_size(self, max_width: Optional[int] = None, max_height: Optional[int] = None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return the preferred (width, height) for this Text including padding (M3準拠).

    Use explicit sizing if provided, otherwise measure text content.
    """
    # Check for explicit sizing first
    w_dim = self.width_sizing
    h_dim = self.height_sizing

    # If both sizing are fixed, return them directly (plus padding)
    if w_dim.kind == "fixed" and h_dim.kind == "fixed":
        l, t, r, b = self.padding
        return (int(w_dim.value) + l + r, int(h_dim.value) + t + b)

    # Otherwise measure the text
    txt = self._resolve_label()
    # Typography comes from the type-scale token.
    font_size = self.type_scale.font_size
    weight = self.type_scale.weight
    tracking = self.type_scale.tracking

    try:
        tf = get_typeface(
            candidate_files=None,
            family_candidates=self._resolve_font_candidates(),
            pkg_font_dir=None,
            fallback_to_default=True,
            weight=weight,
        )

        # Available content width for wrapping: explicit width if fixed,
        # otherwise the constraint handed down by the parent (P0-C). ``0``
        # means unbounded, so soft wrapping stays off.
        l, t, r, b = self.padding
        if w_dim.kind == "fixed":
            avail_w = float(w_dim.value)
        elif max_width is not None:
            avail_w = max(0.0, float(max_width) - float(l) - float(r))
        else:
            avail_w = 0.0

        def measure_w(s: str) -> float:
            return float(measure_text_width(tf, font_size, str(s), tracking))

        lines, _ = self._layout_lines(txt, avail_w, measure_w)

        # Use advance width (the same metric paint uses for wrapping) and
        # round up, so a Text allocated its own preferred width never wraps
        # against itself due to an ink-vs-advance rounding gap.
        measured_width = 0
        for ln in lines:
            measured_width = max(measured_width, int(math.ceil(measure_w(ln))))
        if measured_width <= 0:
            measured_width = max(0, int(font_size * max(1, len(txt) * 0.6)))

        n_lines = max(1, len(lines))
        if n_lines == 1:
            # Preserve prior single-line ink-based height.
            sl, st, sr, sb = measure_text_ink_bounds(tf, font_size, lines[0] if lines else txt, tracking)
            measured_height = int(max(0.0, sb - st))
            if measured_height <= 0:
                measured_height = int(font_size)
        else:
            line_h = float(self.type_scale.line_height)
            measured_height = int(round(line_h * n_lines))
    except Exception:
        exception_once(_logger, "text_preferred_size_measure_exc", "Text preferred_size measurement failed")
        # Fallback: approximate character width ~0.6 * font_size
        approx_char_w = int(font_size * 0.6)
        measured_width = len(txt) * approx_char_w
        measured_height = int(font_size)

    # Apply explicit sizing where provided
    if w_dim.kind == "fixed":
        width = int(w_dim.value)
    else:
        width = measured_width

    if h_dim.kind == "fixed":
        height = int(h_dim.value)
    else:
        height = measured_height

    # The allocated rect is the text plus its padding.
    l, t, r, b = self.padding
    total_w = int(width) + int(l) + int(r)
    total_h = int(height) + int(t) + int(b)

    if max_width is not None:
        total_w = min(int(total_w), int(max_width))
    if max_height is not None:
        total_h = min(int(total_h), int(max_height))

    return (int(total_w), int(total_h))

Paint text with padding, multi-line layout and overflow support.

Source code in src/nuiitivet/widgets/text.py 
@replay_safe
def paint(self, canvas, x: int, y: int, width: int, height: int):
    """Paint text with padding, multi-line layout and overflow support."""
    cx, cy, cw, ch = self.content_rect(x, y, width, height)

    txt = self._resolve_label()
    type_scale = self.type_scale
    font_size = type_scale.font_size
    weight = type_scale.weight
    tracking = type_scale.tracking
    # A parent recolours its label by replacing the style object.
    look = self._look.get(self, (self._style, get_default_font_fallbacks()), self._resolve_look)
    tf = look.typeface
    alignment = self._alignment

    # The key holds every input of line breaking and truncation. The
    # typeface is compared by identity beside it.
    cache_key = (
        txt,
        int(cw),
        int(ch),
        float(font_size),
        int(weight),
        float(tracking),
        self._overflow,
        self._truncation,
        bool(self._soft_wrap),
        self._max_lines if self._max_lines is not None else -1,
        alignment,
        tuple(self.padding),
    )
    cache = self._paint_cache
    if cache is None or cache.key != cache_key or cache.typeface is not tf:
        cache = self._build_paint_cache(cache_key, tf, txt, float(cw), font_size, tracking)
        self._paint_cache = cache

    runs = cache.runs
    if not runs or canvas is None:
        return
    paint = shared_paint(look.color)
    if paint is None:
        return

    clip = self._overflow == "clip"
    if clip:
        canvas.save()
        canvas.clipRect(make_rect(cx, cy, cw, ch))

    if len(runs) == 1:
        self._paint_single_line(canvas, runs[0], cx, cy, cw, ch, alignment, paint)
    else:
        self._paint_multi_line(canvas, cache, cx, cy, cw, ch, alignment, paint)

    if clip:
        canvas.restore()

Source code in src/nuiitivet/widgets/icon.py 
def draw_blob(self, canvas: Any, blob: Any, color: ColorSpec, x: int, y: int, width: int, height: int):
    """Draw a text blob centered in the content area."""
    if blob is None:
        return

    cx, cy, cw, ch = self.content_rect(x, y, width, height)

    try:
        bounds = blob.bounds()
        tx = cx + (cw - bounds.width()) / 2 - bounds.left()
        ty = cy + (ch - bounds.height()) / 2 - bounds.top()
    except Exception:
        exception_once(logger, "icon_base_blob_bounds_exc", "Failed to get blob bounds")
        return

    try:
        from nuiitivet.theme.theme import Theme

        rgba = resolve_color_to_rgba(color, theme=Theme.of(self))
        paint = make_paint(color=rgba, style="fill", aa=True)
    except Exception:
        exception_once(logger, "icon_base_resolve_color_exc", "Failed to resolve icon color")
        return

    if paint is None:
        return

    try:
        canvas.drawTextBlob(blob, tx, ty, paint)
    except Exception:
        exception_once(logger, "icon_base_draw_text_blob_exc", "drawTextBlob failed")

Module Role runtime/window.py Window: the lifecycle state, the root factory, the chrome, the modal gates in the dispatch, the close action, the frame; WindowScope runtime/app.py the registry and the current app (The App) backends/pyglet/runner.py delivers the OS events (The Runner) navigation/navigator.py the root navigator, one per window (NAVIGATION.md) overlay/overlay.py the overlay, one per window (OVERLAY.md) runtime/chrome.py the OS title bar, or a header drawn in the tree layout/geometry.py the root Geometry (GEOMETRY.md) menubar/controller.py the menu bar, one per window (MENU_BAR.md) platform/ime.py the IME geometry, one per window (TEXT_EDITING.md) widgeting/context_lookup.py the ancestor search behind Window.of the app's code opens, closes and operates windows

docs.title: A window opens
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as the app's code
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant N as navigation/navigator.py
    participant O as overlay/overlay.py
    participant A as runtime/app.py

    C->>W: open()
    W->>W: refuse when open, closed, or the parent is not open
    W->>A: current_app(), when not attached
    W->>W: root_factory()
    W->>N: Navigator(content), unless the content is one
    W->>O: overlay_factory()
    W->>W: Stack([navigator, overlay]), the chrome, AppScope > WindowScope > Geometry
    W->>W: root.mount(self)
    W->>A: _register_window(self)
    A->>A: _realize_window_hook(window), when the loop runs

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A closed window stays closed. A reload never resurrects one.
  • Every open window's tree is AppScope > WindowScope > Geometry > the content. The scopes make the app and the window findable and do nothing else.
  • Closing a parent closes its children first, transitively.
  • A window blocked by an open modal child consumes keyboard input. It drops pointer input. The gates sit in the dispatch entry points, below every OS event path.

docs.title: The Runner
docs.text: The pyglet runner owns the process-wide setup and the loop. It turns each open Window into an OS window.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]
    loop[backends/pyglet/event_loop.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    app[runtime/app.py]
    clock[observable/runtime.py]
    pyglet[pyglet]
    callbacks[widgeting/callbacks.py]

    app -- "run_app(app, draw_fps, renderer)" --> runner
    runner -- "ResponsiveEventLoop(draw, fps, keep_running_without_windows) · run()" --> loop
    runner -- "set_ui_thread() · set_clock(clock)" --> clock
    runner -- "_realize_window_hook = _realize · _event_loop · _install_tray() · _uninstall_tray()" --> app
    runner -- "pyglet.window.Window(...) · the event handlers · the GPU context · the IME and first-mouse patches" --> pyglet
    runner -- "_render_frame(dt) · _dispatch_*(...) · _handle_close_request() · _on_window_created() · _set_os_active(active)" --> window
    runner -- "drop_pending_tasks()" --> callbacks
Module Role backends/pyglet/runner.py run_app: the DPI awareness, the clock, the loop, the realise hook, the tray; _realize_window: the pyglet window, its event wiring, the per-window GPU state, the patches backends/pyglet/event_loop.py ResponsiveEventLoop: draws the open windows on demand, keeps running without windows when told to (RENDERING_PIPELINE.md) runtime/window.py the host protocol the OS events are dispatched into (The Window) runtime/app.py the windows to realise, the hook for later ones (The App) observable/runtime.py the UI thread and the clock (OBSERVABLE.md) pyglet the windows, the GL context, the events widgeting/callbacks.py the async work left pending when the loop ends (ASYNCIO_INTEGRATION.md)

docs.title: The loop starts and ends
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as runtime/app.py
    participant R as backends/pyglet/runner.py
    participant K as observable/runtime.py
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant L as backends/pyglet/event_loop.py
    participant Cb as widgeting/callbacks.py

    A->>R: run_app(app, draw_fps, renderer)
    R->>K: set_ui_thread(), set_clock(pyglet.clock)
    R->>L: ResponsiveEventLoop(draw, fps, keep_running_without_windows)
    R->>K: set_clock(event_loop.clock)
    R->>A: _realize_window_hook = _realize
    loop each window open so far, in open order
        R->>R: _realize_window(app, win, event_loop)
        R->>W: _on_window_created()
    end
    R->>A: _install_tray()
    R->>L: run()
    Note over L: the loop ended
    R->>Cb: drop_pending_tasks()
    R->>A: _uninstall_tray(), _realize_window_hook = None

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The UI thread is the thread that installs the clock.
  • Every open window has an OS window while the loop runs.
  • A window's OS events enter the Window's dispatch methods. Nothing in the runner reads the tree.

docs.title: Asyncio Integration
docs.text: The framework owns the asyncio runtime. Application code writes await without managing an event loop.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Two groups of modules take part, with the awaitables the framework hands out at their edges.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    loop[The Loop]
    tasks[The Tasks]
    overlay[overlay/overlay.py]
    navigation[navigation/navigator.py]
    switched[observable/switched.py]
    app[the app]

    app -- "async def on_click(): await ..." --> tasks
    app -- "await overlay.dialog(...) · await handle" --> overlay
    tasks -- "create_task(coro), on the running loop" --> loop
    loop -- "start_pending_tasks(), on entry" --> tasks
    overlay -- "a future per entry · spawn_task(dismiss)" --> tasks
    navigation -- "spawn_task(pop)" --> tasks
    switched -- "spawn_task(run), for a coroutine fn" --> tasks
Module Role The Loop pumps the platform loop inside an asyncio loop The Tasks the running tasks, and the work kept until a loop runs overlay/overlay.py an awaitable handle per entry (OVERLAY.md) navigation/navigator.py an awaited pop, gated on will_pop (NAVIGATION.md) observable/switched.py a coroutine fn run as a task (CONCURRENCY_MODEL.md) the app writes async handlers and awaits the framework's futures

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• An async handler runs on the UI thread.
  • Every task the framework creates is born in spawn_task.

docs.title: The Loop
docs.text: On the desktop ResponsiveEventLoop.run_async pumps pyglet inside an asyncio loop. In a browser the page's own loop drives asyncio.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    loop[backends/pyglet/event_loop.py]
    callbacks[widgeting/callbacks.py]
    pyglet[pyglet]
    asyncio[asyncio]
    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]

    runner -- "run()" --> loop
    loop -- "asyncio.run(run_async())" --> asyncio
    loop -- "start_pending_tasks(), on entry · drop_pending_tasks(), under the sync loop" --> callbacks
    loop -- "platform_event_loop.step(0) · dispatch the window events" --> pyglet
    loop -- "await asyncio.sleep(min(timeout, 0.016))" --> asyncio
Module Role backends/pyglet/event_loop.py pumps pyglet inside an asyncio loop, or runs synchronously as a fallback widgeting/callbacks.py the work kept until a loop runs (The Tasks) pyglet the platform events and the windows asyncio the loop the pump runs inside backends/pyglet/runner.py starts the loop (APP_WINDOW.md)

docs.title: The pump yields between frames
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as backends/pyglet/runner.py
    participant L as backends/pyglet/event_loop.py
    participant A as asyncio
    participant C as widgeting/callbacks.py
    participant P as pyglet

    R->>L: run()
    L->>A: asyncio.run(run_async())
    L->>C: start_pending_tasks()
    loop each iteration
        L->>P: the window events, a frame when pending
        L->>A: await asyncio.sleep(at most 16 ms)
        Note over A: the other tasks run
        L->>P: step(0)
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text: • Under the synchronous loop an await on a framework future never completes.

docs.title: The Tasks
docs.text: widgeting/callbacks.py turns an awaitable a handler returned into a task, or keeps it until a loop runs.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    callbacks[widgeting/callbacks.py]
    batching[observable/batching.py]
    asyncio[asyncio]
    loop[backends/pyglet/event_loop.py]
    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    harness[testing/plugin.py]
    widgets[the widgets and modifiers]
    app[the app]

    widgets -- "invoke_event_handler(cb, args, error_key, error_msg, owner_name)" --> callbacks
    callbacks -- "cb(args)" --> app
    callbacks -- "detach_batch()" --> batching
    callbacks -- "get_running_loop() · create_task(coro)" --> asyncio
    loop -- "start_pending_tasks()" --> callbacks
    runner & loop & window -- "drop_pending_tasks()" --> callbacks
    harness -- "_task_observers · _error_sinks" --> callbacks
Module Role widgeting/callbacks.py turns a handler's awaitable into a task, or keeps it as a PendingTask until a loop runs; the hooks a harness observes through observable/batching.py the batch the task detaches from (OBSERVABLE.md) asyncio the running loop backends/pyglet/event_loop.py starts the kept work on entry (The Loop) backends/pyglet/runner.py drops the kept work after the loop (APP_WINDOW.md) runtime/window.py drops the kept work after a headless render (APP_WINDOW.md) testing/plugin.py observes every task and every contained error (CONCURRENCY_MODEL.md) the widgets and modifiers invoke the app's handlers the app the handler, sync or async

docs.title: An async handler is invoked
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Wd as the widgets and modifiers
    participant C as widgeting/callbacks.py
    participant A as the app
    participant B as observable/batching.py
    participant L as asyncio

    Wd->>C: invoke_event_handler(cb, ...)
    C->>A: cb(args)
    A-->>C: an awaitable
    alt a loop is running
        C->>L: create_task(wrapper)
        L->>C: the wrapper runs
        C->>B: detach_batch()
        C->>A: await the awaitable
    else no loop yet, under a test harness
        C->>C: close the coroutine, raise UnschedulableAsyncWork
    else no loop yet
        C->>C: PendingTask(coro), kept in spawn order
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A task detaches from the batch of the dispatch that started it.
  • An exception in a task is contained.
  • Kept work is dropped where no loop will come.
  • Under a test harness, an exception in a task is re-raised.

docs.title: Box Model
docs.text: A parent hands a widget an allocated rect. The widget's padding insets it to the content rect. A widget may paint past the allocated rect and reports how far.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Four modules give the rects their meaning: the kernel every widget is built on, the box that paints a surface, the MD3 component, and the scroll viewport that displaces its content.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    kernel[The Kernel]
    box[The Box]
    component[The Component]
    viewport[The Viewport]
    layout[layout/]
    window[runtime/window.py]

    layout -- "preferred_size(max_w, max_h) · layout(w, h) · set_layout_rect(x, y, w, h)" --> kernel
    window -- "root.hit_test(x, y)" --> kernel
    box -- "is a" --> kernel
    component -- "is a" --> box
    viewport -- "is a · hit_test(x, y) with the offset undone" --> kernel
    kernel -- "visual_offset()" --> viewport
Module Role The Kernel the rects, the padding, the hit resolution, the overflow contract The Box a painted surface, a clip, a shadow The Component an MD3 container drawn inside the padding The Viewport content painted displaced and clipped layout/ the containers that allocate rects (LAYOUT.md) runtime/window.py the pointer dispatch (INTERACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Widget.padding means allocated rect to content rect, on every widget.
  • Outsets take part in neither layout nor hit testing.
  • Hit testing reads layout state, never paint state.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    padding[rendering/padding.py]
    input[widgeting/widget_input.py]
    participation[widgeting/hit_participation.py]
    transform[modifiers/transform.py]
    bounds[rendering/visual_bounds.py]
    utils[layout/layout_utils.py]
    cache[rendering/skia/paint_cache.py]
    layout[layout/]

    kernel -- "parse_padding(pad)" --> padding
    layout -- "preferred_size(max_w, max_h) · layout(w, h) · set_layout_rect(x, y, w, h)" --> kernel
    kernel -- "_hit_is_interactive()" --> input
    participation -- "is a · descend_children · self_opaque" --> kernel
    transform -- "is a · paint_outsets()" --> kernel
    transform -- "transformed_outsets(w, h, translate, scale, rotation, origin)" --> bounds
    utils -- "paint_outsets() · layout_rect" --> kernel
    cache -- "paint_outsets()" --> kernel
Module Role widgeting/widget_kernel.py the padding and the two rects; hit_test, which descends into the children and then asks the widget's own surface; global_visual_rect; the base paint_outsets, zero rendering/padding.py the four-tuple from a number, a pair or a tuple widgeting/widget_input.py answers whether the widget handles pointer or scroll input (INTERACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md) widgeting/hit_participation.py the explicit hit postures (HIT_TESTING.md) modifiers/transform.py reports where the transformed corners land (MODIFIER.md) rendering/visual_bounds.py the bounding box of a rect under a transform layout/layout_utils.py skips a child whose rect plus outsets lies outside the clip, with a slack band (PAINT_CACHE.md) rendering/skia/paint_cache.py sizes a widget's cache to its rect plus outsets (PAINT_CACHE.md) layout/ the containers (LAYOUT.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Every widget that occupies a rect of its own has padding. preferred_size includes it.
  • What a widget draws goes inside the content rect.
  • A layout box or a leaf hit-tests on its allocated rect.
  • A widget that paints outside its allocated rect reports the overflow in paint_outsets(). Outsets are reported per widget, not per subtree.
  • global_visual_rect is the layout rect plus every ancestor's visual_offset(). Input bounds and overlay anchors read it, never last_rect.

docs.title: The Box
docs.text: Box paints a background, a border and a shadow on its allocated rect.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    box[widgets/box.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    shadow[rendering/shadow.py]
    clip[modifiers/clip.py]
    corner[modifiers/corner_radius.py]
    decoration[modifiers/background.py · border.py · shadow.py]

    box -- "is a · _hit_self_opaque() · paint_outsets() · hit_test(x, y)" --> kernel
    box -- "shadow_outsets(layers)" --> shadow
    clip & corner -- "clip_content = True" --> box
    decoration -- "Box(child, background_color, border_width, shadows, ...)" --> box
Module Role widgets/box.py Box: the painted surface, clip_content, the shadow's reach widgeting/widget_kernel.py the base hit resolution and outsets (The Kernel) rendering/shadow.py how far a shadow's layers blur and offset modifiers/clip.py turns the clip on (MODIFIER.md) modifiers/corner_radius.py rounds the corners and turns the clip on modifiers/background.py · border.py · shadow.py wrap a widget in a Box

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A Box with a background, a border or a shadow catches a hit on its own rect. A bare Box defers to its children.
  • With clip_content, a hit outside the box's rect reaches no child.
  • The shadow's reach is the box's outset.

docs.title: The Component
docs.text: InteractiveWidget draws its container on the content rect. The padding band stays transparent.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    iw[material/interactive_widget.py]
    box[widgets/box.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    styles[material/styles/]

    iw -- "is a · paint_outsets()" --> box
    iw -- "content_rect(x, y, w, h) · _in_local_bounds(x, y)" --> kernel
    iw -- "content_insets · min_width · min_height" --> styles
Module Role material/interactive_widget.py InteractiveWidget: the container, the state layer, the border and the focus ring on the content rect; the focus ring's reach widgets/box.py the surface it is built on (The Box) widgeting/widget_kernel.py the content rect (The Kernel) material/styles/ the MD3 tokens: the container's insets and its minimum size (STYLE_THEME.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A component hit-tests on its content rect.
  • A component's internal spacing lives on a style token, never on Widget.padding.
  • The touch target is inside the content rect.
  • The focus ring's reach is the component's outset while it is enabled.

docs.title: The Viewport
docs.text: ScrollViewport paints its content displaced by the scroll offset and clipped to its rect.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    viewport[layout/scroll_viewport.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    box[widgets/box.py]
    perception[_interaction/perception.py]
    overlay[overlay/overlay_position.py]

    viewport -- "is a · hit_test(x, y + offset)" --> kernel
    kernel -- "visual_offset(), each ancestor" --> viewport
    perception -- "visual_offset() · visual_clip_rect(), probed by name" --> viewport & box
    overlay -- "global_visual_rect" --> kernel
Module Role layout/scroll_viewport.py ScrollViewport: the displaced paint, the hit test inside its rect, visual_offset, visual_clip_rect (LAYOUT.md) widgeting/widget_kernel.py global_visual_rect (The Kernel) widgets/box.py publishes its clip rect the same way (The Box) _interaction/perception.py reads where a widget is on screen (DEV_BRIDGE.md) overlay/overlay_position.py anchors a layer to a widget's on-screen rect (OVERLAY.md)

docs.title: A pointer hits a scrolled component
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant K as widget_kernel.py
    participant V as scroll_viewport.py
    participant B as widgets/box.py
    participant C as interactive_widget.py

    W->>K: root.hit_test(x, y)
    K->>V: hit_test(x - rx, y - ry)
    alt outside the viewport rect
        V-->>K: None
    else
        V->>K: hit_test(x, y + offset), the content
        K->>B: hit_test(...), a child
        alt clip_content, and outside the box's rect
            B-->>K: None
        else
            B->>C: hit_test(...), a child
            C->>C: _in_local_bounds: the content rect
            C-->>W: the component, or None
        end
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A descendant receives no pointer event outside the effective visible region, the intersection of every ancestor's.
  • A visible region constrains the subtree only. Padding, content and outsets are unchanged by it.
  • A container that paints its children away from their layout position publishes visual_offset().

docs.title: Concurrency Model
docs.text: The UI runs on one thread. A value produced on another thread reaches the UI through an Observable.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Four groups of modules take part.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    thread[The UI Thread]
    marshal[The Marshal]
    workers[The Workers]
    harness[The Harness]
    tree[the widget tree]
    backend[the backend]

    backend -- "set_ui_thread()" --> thread
    backend -- "set_clock(clock)" --> marshal
    tree -- "assert_ui_thread()" --> thread
    marshal -- "is_ui_thread()" --> thread
    workers -- "obs.value = result, off the UI thread" --> marshal
    marshal -- "the subscribers, on the UI thread" --> tree
    harness -- "set_clock(harness)" --> marshal
Module Role The UI Thread one definition of which thread the UI runs on The Marshal carries an Observable write from any thread onto the UI thread The Workers the places work runs away from the UI thread The Harness runs a test on the UI thread with its own clock the widget tree the subscribers (WIDGET_ARCHITECTURE.md) the backend names the UI thread and installs the clock (APP_WINDOW.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A worker thread never touches a widget.
  • Every value that crosses from a worker to the UI crosses through an Observable.

docs.title: The UI Thread
docs.text: runtime/threading.py holds the one answer to "is this the UI thread".

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    threading[runtime/threading.py]
    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]
    lifecycle[widgeting/widget_lifecycle.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    value[observable/value.py]
    os[os]

    runner -- "set_ui_thread()" --> threading
    lifecycle -- "assert_ui_thread(), in mount and unmount" --> threading
    kernel -- "assert_ui_thread(), in layout and paint" --> threading
    value -- "is_ui_thread()" --> threading
    os -- "register_at_fork: the child's main thread" --> threading
Module Role runtime/threading.py the cached thread ident; set_ui_thread, is_ui_thread, assert_ui_thread backends/pyglet/runner.py names the thread that runs the frame loop (APP_WINDOW.md) widgeting/widget_lifecycle.py asserts at mount and unmount (WIDGET_ARCHITECTURE.md) widgeting/widget_kernel.py asserts at layout and paint (RENDERING_PIPELINE.md) observable/value.py asks on every write (The Marshal) os re-seats the ident after a fork

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The UI thread is the main thread until a backend names another.
  • The thread that installs the clock is the thread the marshal targets.

docs.title: The Marshal
docs.text: An Observable written off the UI thread notifies on the UI thread.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    value[observable/value.py]
    computed[observable/computed.py]
    batching[observable/batching.py]
    clock[observable/runtime.py]
    threading[runtime/threading.py]
    worker[a worker thread]
    tree[the widget tree]

    worker -- "obs.value = v" --> value
    value & computed & batching -- "is_ui_thread()" --> threading
    value & computed & batching -- "schedule_once(_process_pending_update, 0)" --> clock
    clock -- "the tick, on the UI thread" --> value & computed & batching
    value & computed -- "the subscribers" --> tree
Module Role observable/value.py Observable: holds a pending value and the scheduled flag; applies and notifies observable/computed.py ComputedObservable: the same for a derived value observable/batching.py BatchContext: flushes the queued recomputes observable/runtime.py the installed clock (OBSERVABLE.md) runtime/threading.py the thread test (The UI Thread) a worker thread writes a value the widget tree the subscribers

docs.title: An Observable is written
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as a worker thread
    participant V as observable/value.py
    participant Th as runtime/threading.py
    participant K as observable/runtime.py
    participant T as the widget tree

    W->>V: obs.value = 1
    V->>Th: is_ui_thread()
    alt on the UI thread
        V->>V: _apply(1), notify
        V->>T: the subscribers, with 1
    else off the UI thread
        V->>V: _pending_value = 1, scheduled
        V->>K: schedule_once(_process_pending_update, 0)
        W->>V: obs.value = 2
        V->>V: _pending_value = 2, already scheduled
        Note over K: the next tick, on the UI thread
        K->>V: _process_pending_update
        V->>V: _apply(2), notify
        V->>T: the subscribers, with 2
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A write off the UI thread is applied on the next tick. Writes before the tick coalesce to the latest value.
  • A write on the UI thread applies inline.
  • A batch whose observables want the UI thread flushes its recomputes there.

docs.title: The Workers
docs.text: Work leaves the UI thread through switch_map, a @worker or @server function, or a thread the app starts.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    switched[observable/switched.py]
    worker[remote/worker.py]
    function[remote/function.py]
    threads[remote/threads.py]
    process[remote/process.py]
    web[backends/web/]
    callbacks[widgeting/callbacks.py]
    stdthread[threading]
    value[observable/value.py]
    app[the app]

    app -- "source.switch_map(fn)" --> switched
    switched -- "Thread(run), for a plain fn" --> stdthread
    switched -- "spawn_task(run), for a coroutine fn" --> callbacks
    app -- "@worker · @server · await fn(args)" --> worker
    worker -- "is a: RemoteFunction · call(args)" --> function
    function -- "a thread" --> threads
    function -- "a child process, with process=True" --> process
    function -- "a Web Worker, or the server, in a browser" --> web
    switched & function -- "obs.value = result" --> value
    app -- "Thread(target), writing observables" --> stdthread
Module Role observable/switched.py switch_map: a mapped value whose fn takes time to answer (OBSERVABLE.md) remote/worker.py @worker, a function the app awaits that runs away from the UI remote/function.py RemoteFunction, @server: the declared types and the call remote/threads.py the desktop's threads remote/process.py the desktop's child processes backends/web/ the Web Worker and the server call (WEB_TARGET.md) widgeting/callbacks.py the task a coroutine fn runs as (ASYNCIO_INTEGRATION.md) threading the standard library's threads observable/value.py the values the work reports through (The Marshal) the app starts the work

docs.title: A source changes before its run has answered
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as the source, observable/value.py
    participant M as observable/switched.py
    participant R as the run, on its thread
    participant O as the result, observable/value.py

    S->>M: value 1
    M->>R: fn(1, token 1)
    S->>M: value 2
    M->>M: cancel token 1
    M->>R: fn(2, token 2)
    R->>M: the answer to 1
    M->>M: token 1 is stale, discarded
    R->>M: the answer to 2
    M->>O: obs.value = the answer to 2

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A superseded switch_map run publishes nothing.
  • A @worker or @server function shares nothing with its caller. Arguments and the result are copied.

docs.title: The Harness
docs.text: The pytest plugin runs a test on the UI thread. The harness is the clock.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Every entry carries a monotonic seq.
  • A reload entry's changed names the modules whose source bytes changed. A save with identical bytes leaves it empty.
  • The interaction journal records the human only. A synthesised action bypasses the recorder.
  • The interaction journal's vocabulary is the action vocabulary. A semantic event is not recorded.
  • Typed content never enters a journal. A printable key is dropped. A burst of text is one marker.
  • A scroll entry is recorded only for an event a region consumed. A gesture on one region in one direction is one entry.
  • Console output is unchanged by the capture. No handler is added to the root logger.
  • The journal de-duplicates nothing. The verbose switch makes the emit sites record every occurrence.

docs.title: Dev Modes
docs.text: The dev modes run human to app. The human points at a widget in the running app. The dev runner acts on that widget's source: source jump opens the line that built it, comment mode marks it for the agent, layout edit mode rewrites the line. Source jump does not latch; the two modes do. Every bridge surface (DEV_BRIDGE.md) runs the other way, agent to app.
