docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Every chord the dev runner claims starts with Ctrl+Shift.
  • No action of the agent reaches a mode.
  • A layer that consumes an event ends the walk.
  • At most one mode is latched at a time. A latched mode lets the other's chord pass.
  • The dev runner wraps Widget.__init__. The wrap records, for every widget, the chain of frames outside the package and outside any install directory. The record is rebuilt with the tree on reload.
  • Each frame records the span of the executing call. The frame a jump opens and an edit targets is the innermost user frame outside any __init__.
  • A frame records whether it built the widget directly. A pointer on a widget no user call built resolves to the nearest ancestor a user call did build.
  • Every mode paints on the glass, never into the tree. The glass is painted over the tree last painted, in the frame the mode asks for.
  • Each gesture paints in a colour family of its own.

docs.title: A send wakes the agent's wait
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as coding agent
    participant B as dev/bridge.py (worker thread)
    participant Buf as Comments
    participant M as comment mode (UI thread)
    participant H as human

    A->>B: wait_for_comments(since, timeout)
    B->>Buf: wait(since, timeout)
    Note over Buf: blocks on the condition
    H->>M: marks, text
    M->>Buf: add, write, undo
    alt the human presses Send
        H->>M: Send
        M->>Buf: send()
        Note over Buf: every unanswered mark is marked as awaiting an answer, the undo history is cut
        Buf-->>B: woken, True
        B-->>A: satisfied
        A->>B: see_comments
        B->>Buf: payload
        A->>B: answer_comments
        B->>Buf: the answer on the mark
    else the timeout passes, or the app closes the buffer
        Buf-->>B: woken, False
        B-->>A: timed out
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The picker is geometry-only. An idle Overlay reports itself out of the way. Box exposes its clip_content clip to the occlusion check.
  • A mark carries the visible rect, the node's rect intersected with every ancestor clip. The brackets on the glass and the rect handed to the agent are the same rect. An action aims at the visual rect.
  • A region stores only its rect.
  • One Comments per app is shared by the mode on the UI thread, the reload controller after a rebuild and the bridge on its worker threads. Nodes and regions share one ordered list.
  • Members are keyed on object identity. A member a rebuild dropped is matched back by the key-preferring structural path of HOT_RELOAD.md.
  • Every change to the buffer is an undo step. The undo history ends at the last send. An answer is outside it.
  • Only a send, the timeout or the app going down ends a wait. Leaving the mode does not.
  • The interaction journal records none of what a comment carries: rects, on-screen text, the human's words.

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as human
    participant M as dev/layout_edit_mode.py
    participant L as EditLog (dev/source_edit.py)
    participant F as source file
    participant C as dev/controller.py
    participant T as widget tree
    participant Bd as badge (dev/hud.py)

    H->>M: release the drag, or pick from the bar
    M->>L: apply(edit)
    L->>F: write the spans, keep the inverse
    M->>C: request_reload(file)
    C->>C: next UI tick
    C->>T: rebuild from the factory
    alt the reload landed
        C->>L: after_reload(roots)
        L->>T: look up the widgets built at the edit's site
        L-->>Bd: the miss, when there is one
    else the reload failed
        C->>L: reload_failed(traceback)
        L-->>Bd: the failure, blamed on the pending edit
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• During a gesture only the overlay moves.
  • A site with no user frame is refused.
  • A write is a set of spans in one file, or two for a move across containers. Nothing around a span is reformatted.
  • An edit is undone by its inverse spans. The undo is refused when the text they expect has moved. A refusal reaches the badge and never the Comments.
  • What is written is a value, never a delta. A landing value is measured from the live tree.
  • A layout index must name a source span. An order the runner cannot see in one list literal is refused.
  • Alignment is written on the container. A CrossAligned the human wrote is rewritten in place.
  • The handle is the only grab zone for spacing.
  • Spacing is written in the shape its handles stand for. The file's brackets are kept. The sides the drag did not touch are taken from the live widget.
  • A widget declares in editable_parameters() which class each preset keyword is picked from. The choices are that class's classmethods whose parameters are all optional Literals, or its uppercase attributes. default() names the default. nuiitivet.dev imports no design system.
  • What is written is spelled as the destination's module spells it, a preset as a call of its companion class, a GridItem by the name the module imports. No import is added.
  • Whatever expression a keyword holds is replaced whole.
  • A miss, a site that builds nothing, or a failed reload reaches the badge.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: An exception is caught once, at a boundary. Inside the boundary it propagates.

Module Role backends/pyglet/runner.py the window's event handlers, each dispatch in its own try (APP_WINDOW.md) backends/pyglet/event_loop.py the draw callback in a try (RENDERING_PIPELINE.md) runtime/app_events.py pointer delivery, each step in a try (INTERACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md) widgeting/widget_lifecycle.py the lifecycle hooks and the children's mounts, contained (WIDGET_ARCHITECTURE.md) widgeting/callbacks.py invoke_event_handler, containing a handler (ASYNCIO_INTEGRATION.md) observable/_notify.py notifies each subscriber, surviving one that raises (OBSERVABLE.md) common/logging_once.py the record (The Log) the internal modules propagate the app's callbacks may raise

sequenceDiagram

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A callback's exception never unwinds the dispatch it was called from.
  • CancelledError passes through a task boundary.
  • A failure in run_app before the loop starts raises.

docs.title: The Log
docs.text: exception_once and its siblings de-duplicate by a key the call site chooses.

    logging[logging]
    capture[dev/runtime_capture.py]

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The key is a category and a site, chosen by the call site. It is never the message.
  • A different failure at the same site is logged again.
  • The framework adds no logging handler. It calls no basicConfig.
  • Logging never raises.

docs.text: report_contained tells a listening harness that user code raised.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A containment site reports.
  • A sink never raises.
  • A contained exception keeps its type when it reaches a test.
  • One containment is one record.

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text: The parent decides a widget's size in layout. The measurement is recorded as a layout result. This page is how it reaches the code that reads it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three groups of modules carry a measurement from the layout that made it to the code that reads it.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    queue[The Queue]
    providers[The Providers]
    frame[The Frame]
    app[the app]

    providers -- "queue_size_change · add_size_callback" --> queue
    frame -- "flush_size_change_callbacks()" --> queue
    frame -- "Geometry(content)" --> providers
    app -- "Geometry.of(self).size · on_size_changed(callback)" --> providers
    queue -- "callback(size)" --> app
Module Role The Queue holds a measurement between the layout that made it and the frame that reports it The Providers Geometry for a subtree, on_size_changed for one widget The Frame drains the queue at the start of each frame the app the widgets that read a Geometry or carry a size callback

docs.title: Promises
docs.text: • No Observable is written during layout. No size callback runs during layout.

docs.title: The Queue
docs.text: A measurement waits here from the layout that made it to the start of the next frame.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    sizechange[widgeting/widget_size_change.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    geometry[layout/geometry.py]
    scroll[scrolling/controller.py]
    app[the app]

    kernel -- "queue_size_change(widget, size), from set_layout_rect" --> sizechange
    geometry -- "queue_size_change(self, size), from layout" --> sizechange
    scroll -- "queue_deferred_publish(state, publish_metrics, widget)" --> sizechange
    sizechange -- "invalidate(), on the first queued entry" --> kernel
    window -- "flush_size_change_callbacks()" --> sizechange
    sizechange -- "_dispatch_size_change(size)" --> kernel
    kernel -- "callback(size)" --> app

docs.title: A measurement reaches its consumers
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant K as widget_kernel.py
    participant Q as widget_size_change.py
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant S as scrolling/controller.py
    participant C as the app

    Note over K: set_layout_rect(x, y, width, height), from the parent's layout in frame N
    K->>Q: queue_size_change(widget, size)
    Q->>K: invalidate(), on the first entry
    Note over W: frame N+1 starts
    W->>Q: flush_size_change_callbacks()
    Q->>S: publish_metrics(), each deferred publish
    Q->>K: _dispatch_size_change(size), once per widget
    K->>C: callback(size)
    Note over W: the frame continues (The Frame)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A size callback runs once per changed size.
  • A widget dropped or unmounted before the flush is skipped.

docs.title: The Providers
docs.text: Geometry publishes its own measured size to its subtree as an Observable[Size]. on_size_changed reports a widget's size to the widget that carries it.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    geometry[layout/geometry.py]
    modifier[modifiers/size_changed.py]
    lookup[widgeting/context_lookup.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    sizechange[widgeting/widget_size_change.py]
    app[the app]

    geometry -- "layout(cw, ch), the child at its own size" --> app
    geometry -- "queue_size_change(self, size)" --> sizechange
    geometry -- "add_size_callback(_publish_size)" --> kernel
    app -- "Geometry.of(self).size" --> geometry
    geometry -- "find_provider(context, Geometry)" --> lookup
    app -- "on_size_changed(callback)" --> modifier
    modifier -- "add_size_callback(callback)" --> kernel
Module Role layout/geometry.py Geometry, a widget around one child, publishing size modifiers/size_changed.py on_size_changed, the callback registered on the widget it is applied to widgeting/context_lookup.py resolves a .of() lookup along the parent chain widgeting/widget_kernel.py the size callbacks a widget holds (The Queue) widgeting/widget_size_change.py the queue (The Queue) the app the child a Geometry lays out, the descendants that read it, the widgets that carry a modifier

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Constraints are not published.
  • size is one Observable, never a width and a height apart.
  • The nearest Geometry wins.
  • on_size_changed adds no node to the tree. It creates no scope.

docs.title: The Frame
docs.text: The window runs the frame the queue was drained for. render_to_png drains the queue again until nothing runs, before it paints.

    binding[widgeting/widget_binding.py]
    builder[widgeting/widget_builder.py]

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant Q as widget_size_change.py
    participant B as widget_binding.py
    participant R as widget_builder.py
    participant T as the widget tree

    W->>B: flush_binding_invalidations()
    W->>R: flush_scope_recompositions()
    W->>T: layout(w, h)
    W->>T: paint(canvas)

docs.title: A snapshot drains the queue before it paints
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant Q as widget_size_change.py
    participant B as widget_binding.py
    participant R as widget_builder.py
    participant T as the widget tree

    Note over W: render_to_png: mount, layout(w, h)

        W->>Q: flush_size_change_callbacks()

        else something ran

            W->>R: flush_scope_recompositions()

    W->>T: paint(canvas)
    Note over W: unmount

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The live frame runs no size callback between layout and paint.
  • A snapshot paints after a bounded number of drains.
  • The window wraps the content in a Geometry.

docs.title: Hit Testing
docs.text: Hit testing names the widget under a point. Two axes decide it for every widget. One is whether the widget's own rectangle catches. The other is whether the test descends into its children.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three groups of modules take part, with the pointer dispatch and the overlay at their edges.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    resolution[The Resolution]
    box[The Participation Box]
    postures[The Postures]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    overlay[overlay/overlay.py]
    app[the app]

    window -- "root.hit_test(x, y)" --> resolution
    box -- "_hit_test_children(x, y) · _resolve_hit(x, y, child_hit, self_opaque)" --> resolution
    postures -- "HitParticipationBox(child, condition, descend_children, self_opaque)" --> box
    overlay -- "HitParticipationBox(child, condition, descend_children, self_opaque)" --> box
    app -- "defer_pointer() · block_pointer() · absorb_pointer() · passthrough_pointer()" --> postures
Module Role The Resolution the descent into the children and the widget's own surface The Participation Box one wrapper that fixes both axes while a condition holds The Postures the four modifiers, each a setting of the box runtime/window.py asks for the target of a pointer event (INTERACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md) overlay/overlay.py builds its blocking and click-through layers from the box (OVERLAY.md) the app picks a posture

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The hit region is the rectangle, never the painted shape.
  • The two axes are not public. A posture is named, never spelled as flags.
  • Every widget's hit resolves through _resolve_hit.

docs.title: The Resolution
docs.text: WidgetKernel.hit_test combines the children's answer with the widget's own surface.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    input[widgeting/widget_input.py]
    box[widgets/box.py]
    iw[material/interactive_widget.py]
    deck[layout/deck.py]
    position[overlay/overlay_position.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    children[the child widgets]

    window -- "root.hit_test(x, y)" --> kernel
    kernel -- "hit_test(x - rx, y - ry), topmost first" --> children
    kernel -- "_hit_is_interactive()" --> input
    box -- "is a · _hit_self_opaque(): a painted surface" --> kernel
    iw -- "is a · _in_local_bounds(x, y): the content rect" --> box
    deck & position -- "_resolve_hit(x, y, child_hit, self_opaque=False)" --> kernel
Module Role widgeting/widget_kernel.py the descent, the own-surface policy and the bounds test widgeting/widget_input.py answers whether the widget handles pointer or scroll input (INTERACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md) widgets/box.py catches on its own surface when it paints a background, a border or a shadow (BOX_MODEL.md) material/interactive_widget.py bounds the hit to its content rect (BOX_MODEL.md) layout/deck.py a pure pass-through wrapper (LAYOUT.md) overlay/overlay_position.py a pure pass-through wrapper (OVERLAY.md) runtime/window.py asks for the target (Overview) the child widgets each a kernel of its own

docs.title: A point is resolved
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant K as widgeting/widget_kernel.py
    participant C as the child widgets

    W->>K: hit_test(x, y)
    loop each child, topmost first
        alt the child has a rect with area
            K->>K: skip the child when the point is outside its rect
            K->>C: hit_test(x - rx, y - ry)
        else
            K->>C: hit_test(x, y), untranslated
        end
    end
    alt a child caught
        K-->>W: that widget
    else the widget handles input or paints a surface, and the point is in its bounds
        K-->>W: the widget
    else
        K-->>W: None
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A widget that handles pointer or scroll input catches its rect. A widget that paints a surface catches its rect. Any other widget defers to its children.
  • A size-less provider such as ForEach is no bounds gate for the subtree it lifts into its parent.
  • A pure pass-through wrapper passes self_opaque=False. No wrapper keeps an is self check of its own.

docs.title: The Participation Box
docs.text: HitParticipationBox overrides a subtree's two axes while its condition holds.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    box[widgeting/hit_participation.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    binding[widgeting/widget_binding.py]
    observable[observable/value.py]
    shortcuts[runtime/shortcut_dispatch.py]
    modifiers[the postures]
    overlay[overlay/overlay.py]

    modifiers & overlay -- "HitParticipationBox(child, condition, descend_children, self_opaque)" --> box
    box -- "child._hit_test_children(x, y) · _resolve_hit(x, y, child_hit, self_opaque)" --> kernel
    box -- "observe(condition, _set_active)" --> binding
    binding -- "subscribe" --> observable
    shortcuts -- "is_inert" --> box
Module Role widgeting/hit_participation.py overrides a subtree's two axes while its condition holds; reports whether the subtree is inert widgeting/widget_kernel.py the resolution the box drives (The Resolution) widgeting/widget_binding.py the subscription to an observable condition (WIDGET_ARCHITECTURE.md) observable/value.py an Observable[bool] condition (OBSERVABLE.md) runtime/shortcut_dispatch.py reads whether a subtree is inert (KEYBOARD_SHORTCUTS.md) the postures the four modifiers that configure the box (The Postures) overlay/overlay.py the backdrop and the blocker (OVERLAY.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• An inactive box resolves as the wrapped widget would alone.
  • The condition is read at construction, never at the first hit.
  • The box descends into the wrapped widget's children, not into the widget. The wrapped widget's own surface is governed by the box.
  • widgeting/hit_participation.py imports no modifier.

docs.title: The Postures
docs.text: Four modifiers name one setting of the box each.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    defer[modifiers/defer_pointer.py]
    block[modifiers/block_pointer.py]
    absorb[modifiers/absorb_pointer.py]
    passthrough[modifiers/passthrough_pointer.py]
    visible[modifiers/visible.py]
    box[widgeting/hit_participation.py]
    app[the app]

    app -- "defer_pointer(condition) · block_pointer(condition) · absorb_pointer(condition) · passthrough_pointer(condition)" --> defer & block & absorb & passthrough
    defer -- "descend_children=True, self_opaque=False" --> box
    block -- "descend_children=True, self_opaque=True" --> box
    absorb -- "descend_children=False, self_opaque=True" --> box
    passthrough -- "descend_children=False, self_opaque=False" --> box
    visible -- "passthrough_pointer(not condition)" --> passthrough
Module Role modifiers/defer_pointer.py self never catches, the children do modifiers/block_pointer.py self catches its whole rect, the children still work modifiers/absorb_pointer.py self catches its whole rect, nothing below it is asked modifiers/passthrough_pointer.py the whole subtree is click-through modifiers/visible.py composes the click-through posture into a hidden widget (MODIFIER.md) widgeting/hit_participation.py the wrapper each posture configures (The Participation Box) the app picks a posture, with a bool or an Observable[bool]

docs.title: Two stacked postures resolve a point
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant O as hit_participation.py, the outer box
    participant I as hit_participation.py, the inner box
    participant K as widgeting/widget_kernel.py

    O->>O: hit_test(x, y)
    alt the outer box descends
        O->>I: hit_test(x, y), through the wrapped widget's children
        I->>K: _resolve_hit(x, y, child_hit, self_opaque of the inner)
        I-->>O: the inner answer
    else
        Note over I: never asked
    end
    O->>K: _resolve_hit(x, y, child_hit, self_opaque of the outer)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text: • Stacked postures are nested boxes, the later in a | b outermost. The outermost box decides whether descent happens. Where two disagree on the widget's own surface, the outermost wins.

docs.title: Hot Reload
docs.text: A save rebuilds the content tree from the root factory while the process, the window, the GL context and the app's Observable values survive. The dev bridge that drives the reloaded app is in DEV_BRIDGE.md; the layout edit that lands through a reload is in DEV_MODES.md.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three groups of modules take part: the runner that starts the app, the controller that turns a save into a reload, and the snapshots that carry state into the new tree.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    runner[The Runner]
    controller[The Controller]
    snapshots[The Snapshots]
    tree[the widget tree]
    comments[dev/comments.py]
    edits[dev/source_edit.py]

    runner -- "the app and the root factory" --> controller
    controller -- "snapshot · restore" --> snapshots
    controller -- "rebuild · commit" --> tree
    snapshots -- "read the old tree · write the new one" --> tree
    controller -- "restore(new root)" --> comments
    controller -- "after_reload · reload_failed" --> edits
Module Role The Runner starts the app under the dev session and keeps the root factory The Controller turns a save into one reload: modules, rebuild, commit, the report The Snapshots copy what the old tree held into the new one the widget tree what is rebuilt and restored dev/comments.py the comment marks, matched back after a rebuild (DEV_MODES.md) dev/source_edit.py the pending layout edit, checked after a reload (DEV_MODES.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• User code carries no dev/prod branch.
  • The tree is rebuilt only by re-invoking the root factory.
  • The framework's own modules are never reloaded.

docs.title: The Runner
docs.text: The dev runner imports the user's module, calls main(), and takes the app and its root factory from App.run().

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    main[dev/__main__.py]
    loader[dev/loader.py]
    session[dev/session.py]
    module[the user module]
    app[runtime/app.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    controller[dev/controller.py]

    main -- "set_dev_session(DevSession())" --> session
    main -- "load_app_module · resolve_entry" --> loader -- "import under the real name" --> module
    main -- "main()" --> module -- "App(Window(content=factory)).run()" --> app
    app -- "attach(app, root_factory)" --> session
    window -. "_root_factory · _hot_reload_inert" .-> app
    session -- "the app and the factory" --> controller
Module Role dev/__main__.py parses the command, sets the app's sys.argv, drives the loop dev/loader.py turns the launch target into a real module name, puts the package root on sys.path, finds the entry dev/session.py the process-global DevSession the app attaches to the user module the app's own code, with its main() runtime/app.py App.run() hands the app to the session when one is installed runtime/window.py holds the root factory, or marks the window inert (The Controller) dev/controller.py receives the app and the factory (The Controller)

docs.title: The app starts under the runner
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as dev runner
    participant M as user module
    participant A as App.run()
    participant S as dev session

    R->>S: install
    R->>R: sys.argv = the app's
    R->>M: import under its real name
    R->>M: main(), once
    M->>A: App(Window(content=factory)).run()
    A->>S: attach(app, factory), return without blocking
    R->>R: drive the loop, watch files, reload

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• main() runs once per process.
  • The user's module is imported under its real name, never __main__.
  • The app sees its own sys.argv. The runner's is never restored.
  • A window whose content or overlay is a widget instance is inert to reload.

docs.title: The Controller
docs.text: One save becomes one reload on the UI thread.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    watcher[dev/watcher.py]
    ctrl[dev/controller.py]
    reloader[dev/reloader.py]
    pool[remote/worker.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    error[dev/error_overlay.py]
    journal[dev/journal.py]
    snap[dev/snapshot.py]
    navsnap[dev/navigation_snapshot.py]
    ovsnap[dev/overlay_snapshot.py]
    comments[dev/comments.py]
    edits[dev/source_edit.py]

    watcher -- "_pending.set() from the poll thread" --> ctrl
    ctrl -- "reload_user_modules(project_root, old_factory)" --> reloader
    ctrl -- "retire_pool()" --> pool
    ctrl -- "_rebuild_content_root · _commit_content_root" --> window
    ctrl -- "snapshot_observables · restore_observables" --> snap
    ctrl -- "snapshot_navigation · restore_navigation" --> navsnap
    ctrl -- "snapshot_overlay · restore_overlay" --> ovsnap
    ctrl -- "restore(root)" --> comments
    ctrl -- "after_reload · reload_failed" --> edits
    ctrl -- "show_reload_error · clear_reload_error" --> error
    ctrl -- "record_success · record_error" --> journal
Module Role dev/watcher.py polls the user files' mtimes on a background thread; acknowledges a file the runner wrote dev/controller.py holds the pending event, runs the reload on the UI tick in order dev/reloader.py decides which modules are the user's, orders them, reloads them, re-fetches the factory remote/worker.py the worker pool the reload retires runtime/window.py rebuilds the content root from the factory and commits it in place of the old one dev/error_overlay.py the banner over the still-running UI dev/journal.py records every reload, success or failure dev/snapshot.py, dev/navigation_snapshot.py, dev/overlay_snapshot.py the three snapshots and their restores (The Snapshots) dev/comments.py the comment marks matched back onto the new tree dev/source_edit.py the pending layout edit checked after the reload

docs.title: A save becomes a reload
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant F as watcher thread
    participant C as controller (UI tick)
    participant R as reloader
    participant P as worker pool
    participant W as Window
    participant Snap as the snapshot modules
    participant Cm as Comments
    participant L as EditLog
    participant E as error overlay
    participant J as journal

    F->>C: _pending.set()
    C->>Snap: snapshot observables, snapshot navigation
    C->>R: reload_user_modules(project_root, old_factory)
    R-->>C: the reloaded modules, the re-fetched factory
    C->>P: retire_pool()
    C->>W: _rebuild_content_root(new_factory)
    alt the reload or the rebuild raised
        C->>J: record the error
        C->>E: show the banner, traceback to stderr
        C->>L: reload_failed(traceback)
    else built
        C->>Snap: snapshot overlay
        C->>W: _commit_content_root: unmount the old tree, clear interaction state, mount the new
        C->>Snap: restore overlay, restore observables, restore navigation
        C->>Cm: restore(new root)
        C->>E: clear the banner
        C->>L: after_reload(roots)
        C->>J: record success
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A user module lies under the project root, outside the install directories, under none of the blacklisted root packages.
  • Every user module is reloaded on every save.
  • The factory is re-fetched by name from its reloaded module.
  • Only the content tree is rebuilt.
  • A reload or a rebuild that raises leaves the previous tree on screen.
  • No reference into the old tree survives the commit.
  • The watcher only signals.

docs.title: The Snapshots
docs.text: The new tree starts with fresh observables, a fresh navigator and a fresh overlay. Each snapshot writes into the new tree what the old one held, matched by an identity that survives the rebuild. The replay of the route stack is in NAVIGATION.md.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    snap[dev/snapshot.py]
    navsnap[dev/navigation_snapshot.py]
    ovsnap[dev/overlay_snapshot.py]
    tree[the widget tree]
    obs[observable/protocols.py]
    navigator[navigation/navigator.py]
    overlay[overlay/overlay.py]

    snap -- "children_snapshot() · built_child · key" --> tree
    snap -- "MutableObservableBase.value, read and written" --> obs
    navsnap -- "snapshot_stack() · restore_stack(log)" --> navigator
    ovsnap -- "snapshot_stack() · restore_stack(records)" --> overlay
Module Role dev/snapshot.py walks the tree by structural path, copies every mutable observable's value, writes it back at the same path dev/navigation_snapshot.py reads the route log before the swap, replays it after the commit dev/overlay_snapshot.py reads the entry records before the commit, shows them again after it the widget tree what the walk reads: children_snapshot(), built_child, key (widgeting/) observable/protocols.py MutableObservableBase, the value the snapshot copies navigation/navigator.py keeps the route log and replays it (NAVIGATION.md) overlay/overlay.py keeps the entry records, replays them, hands the old handle to the new entry (OVERLAY.md)

docs.title: An awaited entry survives a reload
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as controller
    participant OS as dev/overlay_snapshot.py
    participant Old as the overlay before the reload
    participant New as the overlay after the reload
    participant H as the handle the app awaits

    C->>OS: snapshot_overlay()
    OS->>Old: snapshot_stack()
    Note over Old: the returned entries are carried
    C->>OS: restore_overlay(records)
    OS->>New: restore_stack(records), bottom to top
    loop each record
        alt the intent still resolves
            New->>New: replay(overlay, intent) → a new entry
            New->>H: the new entry takes over the future
        else the intent no longer resolves
            New->>H: DISPOSED
        end
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• An observable's value is copied. The object holding it is not.
  • A widget's key is its identity for the restore. A keyless widget is identified by its position and type.
  • A path with no match in the new tree leaves that observable at its initial value.
  • Only observables held by a widget in the tree are restored.
  • An intent is resolved by its qualified name.
  • An awaited handle completes once: by its own entry, by the entry that took it over, or with DISPOSED.
  • An entry shown from a widget is not recorded. It closes with the old tree.
  • The record lives in the core Overlay.
  • An entry whose intent no longer resolves does not stop the entries above it from being restored.

docs.title: Interaction Architecture
docs.text: Pointer events, focus and keyboard input are handled by nodes hosted on a widget.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Five groups of modules take part: the window, the nodes, the hosts that carry nodes, the hooks the Tab walk asks, and the widgets that own a focus scope.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    backend[the backend]
    window[The Window]
    nodes[The Nodes]
    hosts[The Hosts]
    hooks[The Hooks]
    owners[The Owners]

    backend -- "pointer · key · text events" --> window
    window -- "on_pointer_event · handle_key_event · _set_focused" --> nodes
    window -- "blocks_focus_traversal · focus_traversal_children · occluding_content_widget" --> hooks
    hosts -- "add_node · ensure_interaction_region" --> nodes
    owners -- "FocusScope(policy) · request_focus" --> nodes
    nodes -- "request_focus(node, source)" --> window
Module Role the backend delivers pointer, key and text events to the window The Window dispatches the events, holds the focused node, walks the Tab sequence, traps focus in a modal The Nodes the nodes a host carries, the state they share, the scope and its policies The Hosts the ways a widget becomes a host: a modifier wrapping it, or inheriting through Clickable The Hooks what hides or narrows the Tab walk, and the shortcut layer that asks the same hooks The Owners the widgets that traverse their own parts through a scope

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Input reaches a widget only through the nodes on its host.
  • A widget requests focus. Only the window sets it.

docs.title: The Window
docs.text: The window turns backend events into calls on nodes, holds the one focused node, and walks the tree for the Tab sequence.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    backend[the backend]
    window[Window]
    node[FocusNode]
    scope[FocusScope]
    hooks[the hooks]
    overlay[Overlay]
    bindings[runtime/shortcut_dispatch.py]
    navigator[Navigator]

    backend -- "pointer · key · text · IME events" --> window
    window -- "_set_focused(value, source) · notify_focus_source · handle_key_event · handle_text_event" --> node
    window -- "handle_tab(backwards) · on_enter(backwards)" --> scope
    window -- "blocks_focus_traversal · focus_traversal_children" --> hooks
    window -- "occluding_content_widget()" --> overlay
    window -- "a key no node consumed" --> bindings
    window -- "request_back(), on the Escape release" --> navigator
Module Role the backend delivers pointer, key, text and IME events Window dispatches the events, holds the focused node and the last input source, walks the tree from the traversal root for the stops, drops focus the walk no longer reaches, traps focus inside an open modal FocusNode, FocusScope the nodes the window calls (The Nodes) the hooks what the walk asks on the way down (The Hooks) Overlay the occluding entry the walk starts from (The Hooks) runtime/shortcut_dispatch.py the shortcut bindings a key falls to (KEYBOARD_SHORTCUTS.md) Navigator back navigation on Escape (NAVIGATION.md)

docs.title: A Tab press
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Window
    participant Sc as the FocusScope enclosing the focused node
    participant N as the next stop's FocusNode

    W->>Sc: handle_tab(backwards)
    alt the scope handled Tab
        Note over Sc: The Nodes, "A Tab press inside a scope"
    else the scope lets Tab escape, or there is none
        W->>W: _collect_focus_nodes() from the traversal root
        W->>W: the stop after (or before) the focused one, wrapping
        Note over W: a focused node that is no stop resumes from its scope owner's stop
        W->>W: request_focus(next, KEYBOARD)
        W->>N: _set_focused(True, KEYBOARD)
        opt the stop owns a scope
            W->>Sc: on_enter(backwards) on that scope
        end
    end

docs.title: A modal opens and closes
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Window
    participant O as Overlay
    participant F as FocusNode

    Note over W: once per frame
    W->>O: occluding_content_widget()
    O-->>W: the entry's content
    W->>W: remember (entry, the focused node)
    W->>W: request_focus(the first stop inside the entry, _last_input_source)
    W->>F: _set_focused(True, source)
    W->>O: occluding_content_widget()
    O-->>W: nothing
    W->>W: forget the entry, take back the node it remembered
    alt the invoker is still displayed
        W->>W: request_focus(the invoker, _last_input_source)
        W->>F: _set_focused(True, source)
    else the invoker is gone
        W->>W: request_focus(None)
        W->>F: _set_focused(False)
    end

docs.title: A key press reaches its handler
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as backend
    participant W as Window
    participant F as focused FocusNode
    participant P as ancestor FocusNode
    participant S as shortcut bindings

    B->>W: key press
    alt a modal child blocks the window
        W-->>B: consumed, delivered to nobody
    else Tab
        Note over W: "A Tab press"
    else any other key
        W->>F: handle_key_event(key, modifier_keys)
        F->>F: on_key
        F->>P: bubbles while on_key returns False
        P-->>W: False
        W->>S: _dispatch_shortcut, unless the focused chain will type the key
        S-->>W: no binding
        W->>W: default actions
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• One walk yields the reachable widgets. The stops and the reachability of the focused node rest on it.
  • Reachable means not hidden by a blocker, a narrowing container or an input-blocking overlay entry.
  • While an input-blocking overlay entry is open, the sequence starts at that entry's content.
  • Focus is never outside the open entry. Focus is never left in a closed entry.
  • Focus held in content that is no longer reachable is dropped.
  • Scopes resolve innermost first.
  • Every key press and every pointer press sets the window's last input source.
  • A key consumed by one handler reaches no other.
  • A key the focused chain will turn into text never reaches the shortcut bindings.
  • on_text, on_text_motion and on_ime_composition go to the focused node only.
  • Escape is consumed on press. Its release runs back navigation.
  • Key input to a window blocked by a modal child is consumed and delivered to nobody.

docs.title: The Nodes
docs.text: A node is attached to a host and shares the host's InteractionState. The focus node holds focus and keys; the scope groups the nodes beneath it.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    mixin[InteractionHostMixin]
    region[InteractionRegion]
    state[InteractionState]
    pointer[PointerInputNode]
    focus[FocusNode]
    drag[DraggableNode]
    scope[FocusScope]
    policy[FocusTraversalPolicy]
    nodep[FocusNodePolicy]
    virt[VirtualStopPolicy]
    blocker[FocusTraversalBlocker]
    source[FocusSource]
    window[Window]

    region -- "is a" --> mixin
    mixin -- "add_node · get_node · on_pointer_event" --> pointer & focus & drag & scope
    pointer -- "hovered · pressed" --> state
    focus -- "focused" --> state
    pointer -- "request_focus_from_pointer()" --> mixin
    mixin -- "request_focus(POINTER)" --> focus
    focus -- "request_focus(self, source)" --> window
    focus -- "the source of the last focus change" --> source
    focus -- "parent: the nearest ancestor host's FocusNode" --> focus
    scope -- "members · current_index · set_current · entry_index · on_boundary" --> policy
    nodep & virt -- "is a" --> policy
    nodep -- "request_focus(KEYBOARD) on a member" --> focus
    blocker -. "blocks_focus_traversal, implemented by a host" .-> mixin
Module Role InteractionHostMixin carries the nodes, routes a pointer event to them, asks focus for the host on a primary press InteractionRegion the wrapper host a modifier puts around a widget, built once per widget by ensure_interaction_region() InteractionState the one state the nodes write and the widget paints from PointerInputNode hover, press, release, click; captures the pointer on a press FocusNode holds focus, says whether it is a Tab stop, bubbles keys and text to the ancestor node DraggableNode drag start, deltas and end, with long-press initiation FocusScope marks a subtree as one group Tab enters and leaves FocusTraversalPolicy, FocusNodePolicy, VirtualStopPolicy enumerates a scope's members and moves between them; over real child nodes, or over stops the owner keeps FocusTraversalBlocker the protocol a host implements to hide its subtree from the Tab walk FocusSource whether a focus change came from the keyboard or the pointer Window the one that sets focus (The Window)

docs.title: A Tab press inside a scope
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Window
    participant Sc as the innermost FocusScope enclosing the focused node
    participant P as its FocusTraversalPolicy
    participant F as the focused FocusNode

    W->>Sc: handle_tab(backwards)
    alt the scope roves on Tab, and a member lies in that direction
        Sc->>P: set_current(next)
        Sc-->>W: True
        W->>F: notify_focus_source(KEYBOARD)
    else the boundary
        Sc->>P: on_boundary(direction)
        alt the policy consumes Tab
            P-->>W: True
        else the policy lets Tab escape
            P-->>W: False
            Note over W: The Window, "A Tab press"
        end
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The widget paints hovered, pressed, focused and disabled from the host's one InteractionState.
  • A node with traversable=False holds focus, receives keys and bubbles them. The Tab sequence never stops on it.
  • A key the focused node's on_key returns False for bubbles to the nearest ancestor FocusNode.
  • A request for the node already focused re-announces the source. The source changes without focus moving.
  • A scope is the unit Tab enters and leaves. Tab enters at the first member and Shift+Tab at the last, unless the policy's entry_index says otherwise.
  • The members of a FocusNodePolicy are traversable=False. Only the policy moves focus between them.
  • Whether Tab roves between the members, or is always a boundary, is the scope's setting. What happens at the boundary, escape or consume, is the policy's answer.

docs.title: The Hosts
docs.text: A widget becomes a host in one of two ways: a modifier wraps it in an InteractionRegion, or it inherits InteractionHostMixin through Clickable.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    focusable[the interaction modifiers]
    region[InteractionRegion]
    clickable[Clickable]
    interactive[InteractiveWidget]
    mixin[InteractionHostMixin]
    node[FocusNode]

    focusable -- "ensure_interaction_region(widget), once" --> region
    focusable -- "add_node(FocusNode(...)) when none" --> region
    clickable -- "is a" --> mixin
    interactive -- "is a" --> clickable
    clickable -- "FocusNode(traversable=...)" --> node
Module Role the interaction modifiers focusable(), clickable(), hoverable(): wrap any widget in one shared region and add the node each needs Clickable the host every control inherits; carries traversable, and blocks the Tab walk while disabled InteractiveWidget the Material host: the state layer, the focus ring, activation on Space and Enter InteractionRegion, InteractionHostMixin, FocusNode what the hosts are built from (The Nodes)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A modifier wraps the widget in one InteractionRegion. A second pointer modifier on the same widget reuses it.
  • A standard control adds its nodes in __init__. No wrapper enters the tree.
  • A primary-button press on a host with a FocusNode requests focus for it, with the pointer as the source.
  • A new capability is a new node on the same host.

docs.title: The Hooks
docs.text: The Tab walk asks the hooks on the way down.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph blockers["blocks_focus_traversal"]
        collapsible[Collapsible]
        block[block_focus_traversal]
        visible["visible()"]
    end
    subgraph narrowers["focus_traversal_children()"]
        children[Widget]
        deck[Deck]
        navigator[Navigator]
    end
    overlay[Overlay]
    foreground["is_foreground()"]
    walk[Window._iter_focus_traversal]
    root[Window._focus_traversal_root]

    blockers -- "True hides the subtree" --> walk
    narrowers -- "the children to walk" --> walk
    overlay -- "occluding_content_widget(): the entry's content" --> root
    blockers & narrowers -- "the same answers" --> foreground
Module Role Collapsible blocks the walk while closed block_focus_traversal() blocks the walk while its condition holds visible() hides a subtree; composed of block_focus_traversal() and the pointer pass-through Widget focus_traversal_children(): the children to walk, children_snapshot() unless a container narrows it Deck narrows the walk to the selected page Navigator narrows the walk to the top route Overlay occluding_content_widget(): the content of the topmost input-blocking entry, or none is_foreground() the shortcut layer's test of whether a binding's subtree is displayed Window._iter_focus_traversal, Window._focus_traversal_root the walk and its root (The Window)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A blocking FocusTraversalBlocker hides its whole subtree.
  • focus_traversal_children() narrows the walk to some of the children. It is resolved on every call.
  • The shortcut layer's foreground test asks the same hooks as the walk.

docs.title: The Owners
docs.text: A widget that traverses its own parts owns a FocusScope and gives it a policy over its members.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    menu[Menu]
    group[_ButtonGroupBase]
    slider[_RangeSlider]
    radio[RadioGroup]
    rail[NavigationRail]
    radiopolicy[_RadioTraversalPolicy]
    railpolicy[_RailTraversalPolicy]
    nodep[FocusNodePolicy]
    virt[VirtualStopPolicy]
    scope[FocusScope]
    window[Window]

    menu & group -- "FocusScope(FocusNodePolicy(items), tab_roves=False)" --> nodep
    slider -- "FocusScope(VirtualStopPolicy(handles))" --> virt
    radio -- "FocusScope(_RadioTraversalPolicy(self), tab_roves=False)" --> radiopolicy
    rail -- "FocusScope(_RailTraversalPolicy(self), tab_roves=False)" --> railpolicy
    nodep & virt & radiopolicy & railpolicy -- "the policy of" --> scope
    menu -- "request_focus(_last_input_source) on open" --> window
Module Role Menu items as real focus nodes; the arrows rove, Tab is a boundary _ButtonGroupBase items as real focus nodes; Left and Right rove, stopping at the ends _RangeSlider the two handles as virtual stops; Tab roves between them RadioGroup, _RadioTraversalPolicy entered at the selected radio; the arrows rove, wrap, and move the selection NavigationRail, _RailTraversalPolicy entered at the selected item; Up and Down rove and wrap, moving focus only FocusScope, FocusNodePolicy, VirtualStopPolicy what the owners build on (The Nodes) Window hands a self-focusing widget its last input source (The Window)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A group has one external Tab stop, its owner's. A popup menu has none.
  • A disabled member has no FocusNode.
  • Whether roving wraps, and whether it moves the selection, are the policy's decisions.
  • A widget that takes focus on its own inherits the window's last input source.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: A shortcut is a key gesture bound to a command. It fires whether or not anything holds focus.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three groups of modules take part.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    values[The Values]
    binding[The Binding]
    dispatch[The Dispatch]
    backend[the backend]
    app[the app]

    app -- "key_shortcut(spec, on_trigger, scope)" --> binding
    app -- "MenuEntry(shortcut=spec)" --> values
    binding -- "to_shortcut(spec) · ShortcutBinding(shortcut, on_trigger, scope) · shortcut.matches(key, modifier_keys)" --> values
    backend -- "on_key_press(key, modifier_keys)" --> dispatch
    dispatch -- "match(key, modifier_keys, scope) · trigger(binding)" --> binding
    dispatch -- "produces_text(key, modifier_keys)" --> values
    binding -- "on_trigger()" --> app
Module Role The Values the frozen value types The Binding the modifier and the menu bar, ending in a widget's ShortcutNode The Dispatch the key-press tiers in the window the backend the source of key presses (APP_WINDOW.md) the app declares the bindings, owns the commands

docs.title: Promises
docs.text: • A binding lives on a widget. The widget's place in the tree decides whether the binding is live.

docs.title: The Values
docs.text: A gesture, a binding and a scope are frozen values, shared between a menu item and a modifier.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    shortcut[input/shortcut.py]
    codes[input/codes.py]
    menu[menus/model.py]
    keysc[modifiers/key_shortcut.py]
    interaction[widgets/interaction.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]

    shortcut -- "resolve_modifiers(modifiers), at match and display" --> codes
    menu -- "to_shortcut(spec) · shortcut.display" --> shortcut
    keysc -- "to_shortcut(spec) · ShortcutBinding(shortcut, on_trigger, scope)" --> shortcut
    interaction -- "shortcut.matches(key, modifier_keys)" --> shortcut
    window -- "produces_text(key, modifier_keys)" --> shortcut

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• MOD_ACCEL is resolved when a gesture is matched or displayed, never when it is constructed.
  • Both sides of a match pass through normalize_key_name.

docs.title: The Binding
docs.text: A binding reaches a widget through key_shortcut or through a menu bar. Both end in the widget's ShortcutNode.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    keysc[modifiers/key_shortcut.py]
    interaction[widgets/interaction.py]
    bar[menubar/bar.py]
    shortcut[input/shortcut.py]
    app[the app]

    app -- "widget.modifier(key_shortcut(spec, on_trigger, scope))" --> keysc
    bar -- "KeyShortcutModifier(binding).apply(bar)" --> keysc
    keysc -- "ensure_interaction_region(widget) · region.add_node(ShortcutNode()) · node.bind(binding)" --> interaction
    interaction -- "shortcut.matches(key, modifier_keys)" --> shortcut
    interaction -- "binding.on_trigger()" --> app

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A ShortcutNode holds one binding per gesture.
  • A menu item's shortcut is a MOUNT binding on the menu bar.
  • A menu item and a key_shortcut binding reference the command's callback. Neither owns it.

docs.title: The Dispatch
docs.text: The window offers a key press to the focused node first, then to the bindings, narrowest scope first.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    window[runtime/window.py]
    interaction[widgets/interaction.py]
    scopes[runtime/shortcut_dispatch.py]
    overlay[overlay/overlay.py]
    shortcut[input/shortcut.py]
    backend[the backend]
    tree[the widget tree]

    backend -- "on_key_press(key, modifier_keys)" --> window
    window -- "FocusNode.handle_key_event(key, modifier_keys) · accepts_text_input" --> interaction
    window -- "produces_text(key, modifier_keys)" --> shortcut
    window -- "ShortcutNode.match(key, modifier_keys, scope) · trigger(binding)" --> interaction
    window -- "is_foreground(owner)" --> scopes
    scopes -- "Overlay.of(widget, root=True).occluding_content_widget()" --> overlay
    scopes -- "blocks_focus_traversal · is_inert · focus_traversal_children() · _stack.top()" --> tree
    window -- "children_snapshot() · built_child, from the root" --> tree
Module Role runtime/window.py resolves a key press in tiers; collects the ShortcutNodes of the tree widgets/interaction.py the focused FocusNode and the chain it bubbles along (INTERACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md); the ShortcutNodes (The Binding) runtime/shortcut_dispatch.py answers whether a widget is on the topmost interactable layer overlay/overlay.py names the content of the topmost blocking entry (OVERLAY.md) input/shortcut.py produces_text (The Values) the backend the source of key presses (APP_WINDOW.md) the widget tree the ancestors asked whether they hide the widget (INTERACTION_ARCHITECTURE.md)

docs.title: A key press reaches a binding
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as the backend
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant I as widgets/interaction.py
    participant S as shortcut_dispatch.py

    B->>W: on_key_press(key, modifier_keys)
    Note over W: Escape and Tab are handled before this
    W->>I: handle_key_event(key, modifier_keys), the focused node and its ancestors
    alt consumed
        I-->>W: True
    else declined
        W->>I: accepts_text_input
        alt the chain takes text, and produces_text(key, modifier_keys)
            Note over W: no binding is consulted
        else
            W->>I: match(key, modifier_keys, FOCUS), the focused node's ancestors innermost first
            alt one matched
                W->>I: trigger(binding)
            else none
                W->>S: is_foreground(owner), every node in the tree
                W->>I: match(key, modifier_keys, FOREGROUND), the nodes in the foreground
                alt exactly one matched
                    W->>I: trigger(binding)
                else several matched
                    Note over W: warn once, fire none
                else none
                    W->>I: match(key, modifier_keys, MOUNT), every node
                    Note over W: one fires, several warn, none falls through
                end
            end
        end
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A key the focused chain consumes reaches no binding.
  • A key the focused chain can type reaches no binding. When text and a shortcut can both claim a key, the key is text.
  • Among FOCUS bindings the innermost enclosing the focused node wins.
  • Several FOREGROUND or MOUNT matches fire nothing.
  • A widget is in the foreground by the same test that puts it in the Tab sequence.
  • A blocking overlay entry puts everything outside its content out of the foreground. A passthrough entry blocks nothing.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: A widget's size and spacing are its own properties. Its parent places it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Five groups of modules take part, with the Material components and the app at their edges.

docs.text:
flowchart LR
    sizing[The Sizing]
    containers[The Containers]
    composable[The Composable]
    fit[The Fit]
    window[The Window Sizing]
    material[the Material components]
    app[the app]

    containers -- "width_sizing · height_sizing · layout_align · cross_align" --> composable
    material -- "width · length · size, per open axis" --> sizing
    app -- "fit · content_alignment" --> fit
    app -- "Window(width, height, position)" --> window

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• padding and gap are the two spacing properties.
  • A modifier never changes layout (MODIFIER.md).
  • Alignment belongs to the parent.

docs.title: The Sizing
docs.text: A Sizing is how a widget asks for space on one axis.

docs.title: A row shares its width out
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as layout/row.py · column.py
    participant M as layout/measure.py
    participant C as the children

    R->>M: preferred_size(child, max_w, max_h), each child
    R->>R: the fixed and auto children take their size

    R->>C: set_layout_rect(x, y, w, h)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Only the space left after the fixed and auto children is shared by weight.
  • A weight child measures as its content.
  • An axis MD3 leaves open is a constructor parameter, named width, length or size by its degree of freedom. An axis MD3 fixes is a style token.

docs.title: The Containers
docs.text: A container measures its children and allocates each a rect.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Alignment positions a child. It never stretches one.
  • Whether a child fills its Grid cell is the child's own sizing.
  • Nothing clips a child larger than its rect.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text: • A declared value wins. An undeclared one is derived from the built child.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text: • A window position is resolved against the screen's work area, never its bounds. It places the outer frame, never the client area.

docs.title: Material Interaction
docs.text: Every interactive Material widget is an InteractiveWidget.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three groups of modules take part.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Whether a widget is focused and whether it shows a ring are two separate answers.
  • navigation/ and overlay/ import nothing from material/. The Material motion reaches them as a TransitionSpec.

docs.text: InteractiveWidget is a Clickable with the MD3 state layer, the focus ring and the Space and Enter binding.

sequenceDiagram

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Keyboard focus draws no state layer by default.
  • The ring is drawn for keyboard and programmatic focus, never for pointer focus. It follows the latest FocusSource, whether or not focus moved.
  • The ring's reach is the widget's outset (BOX_MODEL.md).

docs.text: Two components draw the focus differently from the base.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A roved menu item layers focus.
  • A rail item keeps the ring alone, inset on the active indicator.

docs.text:
• A spec with no backward variant plays its forward definition on a pop.
  • The barrier fades with the progress where the spec says fade.
  • A painter reads the resolved visual spec and composes nothing else.

docs.title: Menu Bar
docs.text: The menu is a model registered on the window, Window(menu=...). One model feeds the in-app bar on Windows and Linux and the global bar on macOS.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Four groups of modules take part, with the window, the app and the tray at their edges.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    model[The Model]
    controller[The Controller]
    bar[The In-App Bar]
    bridge[The macOS Bridge]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    app[runtime/app.py]
    tray[platform/tray.py]

    window -- "MenuBarController(window, menu) · set_model(model) · install_platform_bridge() · os_focus_changed(active) · window_closed()" --> controller
    bar -- "register_slot(slot) · activate(item)" --> controller
    controller -- "menubar_changed(active, model)" --> bar
    controller -- "MenuBarFocusCoordinator.attach(app) · window_created · focus_changed · model_changed · window_closed" --> bridge
    bridge -- "activate(entry)" --> controller
    controller -- "window.close() · minimize() · maximize() · restore() · full_screen()" --> window
    controller -- "app.exit()" --> app
    bar -- "MenuEntry · MenuBar.style · MenuBarThemeData" --> model
    bridge -- "MenuEntry · MenuBar" --> model
    tray -- "MenuEntry" --> model

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Every surface activates an entry through the controller.
  • Structure is replaced wholesale through window.menu. label, enabled and checked move live on every surface.
  • On each platform exactly one mechanism fires a menu shortcut: the in-app bar's bindings, or the native key equivalents.

docs.title: The Model
docs.text: The entries, the bar root, the style and the palette are plain data, rendered by whichever surface the platform has.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    entry[menus/model.py]
    menubar[menubar/model.py]
    mbstyle[menubar/style.py]
    themedata[menubar/theme_data.py]
    shortcut[input/shortcut.py]
    material[material/theme/material_theme.py]
    plain[theme/plain_theme.py]
    tray[platform/tray.py]
    bar[menubar/bar.py]

    menubar -- "items, a tuple of MenuEntry" --> entry
    menubar -- "style" --> mbstyle
    mbstyle -- "merged_palette(theme_data)" --> themedata
    entry -- "to_shortcut(spec) · shortcut.display" --> shortcut
    material & plain -- "register MenuBarThemeData(ColorSpec tokens)" --> themedata
    tray -- "MenuEntry" --> entry
    bar -- "theme.extension(MenuBarThemeData)" --> themedata

docs.text:
• menus/ imports no surface. menubar/ imports menus/.
  • The palette holds ColorSpec tokens, resolved at paint.
  • MenuBarThemeData and MenuBarStyle live outside material/. The bar reads its palette from Theme.extension(MenuBarThemeData), never from a Material colour role.

docs.text: One controller per window holds the model. Every activation runs through it. It chooses the slot that renders.

    window[runtime/window.py]
    app[runtime/app.py]
    slots[menubar/slots.py]

    builder[menus/nsmenu.py]
    entry[menus/model.py]

    slots -- "register_slot(slot) · unregister_slot(slot)" --> controller
    controller -- "menubar_changed(active, model)" --> slots
    bar -- "activate(item)" --> controller
    builder -- "activate(entry)" --> controller
    controller -- "MenuBarFocusCoordinator.attach(window.app) · window_created · focus_changed · model_changed · window_closed" --> focus
    controller -- "NSMenuBridge.is_supported()" --> nsmenu
    controller -- "checked.value = not checked.value · on_select()" --> entry

docs.title: An entry is activated
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as bar.py, or menus/nsmenu.py
    participant C as controller.py
    participant E as menus/model.py
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant A as runtime/app.py

    S->>C: activate(item)
    opt item.checked is an Observable
        C->>E: checked.value = not checked.value
    end
    alt item.role is QUIT
        C->>A: exit()
    else another standard role
        C->>W: the role's method
    else item.on_select is set
        C->>E: on_select(), exceptions contained
    end

docs.title: The slot that renders is chosen
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as slots.py
    participant C as controller.py

    S->>C: register_slot(slot), on mount
    alt a platform bridge is attached
        Note over C: no slot is active
    else a user area is mounted
        Note over C: the first mounted area is active, the rest are inert, warned once
    else
        Note over C: the most recently mounted default slot is active
    end
    C->>S: menubar_changed(active, model), every registered slot

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A window-scoped role calls the owning window. QUIT calls that window's app.
  • A disabled entry is never activated by a shortcut.
  • The model stays on the window wherever it renders.
  • A mounted user area takes over from the default slot.

docs.title: The In-App Bar
docs.text: On Windows and Linux a slot builds the bar widget. A top-level entry opens a popup through the overlay.

flowchart LR
    slots[menubar/slots.py]
    bar[menubar/bar.py]
    controller[menubar/controller.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    menu[material/menu.py]
    overlay[overlay/overlay.py]
    keysc[modifiers/key_shortcut.py]

    entry[menus/model.py]

    slots -- "register_slot(self) · unregister_slot(self)" --> controller
    controller -- "menubar_changed(active, model)" --> slots
    slots -- "MenuBarWidget(model), at build when active" --> bar

docs.title: A top-level menu opens and closes
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as bar.py
    participant E as menus/model.py
    participant O as overlay.py
    participant M as material/menu.py

    B->>B: close_menu(), the open popup if any
    B->>M: Menu(entries, on_dismiss=close_menu, style), from the entry's submenu
    B->>O: show(popup, passthrough=False, dismiss_on_outside_tap=True, anchored under the title)
    B->>E: subscribe to label, enabled and checked of the open entries
    alt an item is clicked
        M->>B: activate(item)
        B->>B: close_menu(): handle.close(), dispose the subscriptions
    else an outside tap
        O->>M: unmount
        M->>B: popup_gone(popup)
        B->>O: handle.done()
        O-->>B: True
        B->>B: close_menu()
    else the overlay host remounts
        O->>M: unmount
        M->>B: popup_gone(popup)
        B->>O: handle.done()
        O-->>B: False, the popup stays open
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The popups are the MD3 Menu widgets. Their MenuStyle is derived from the bar's palette, never from the Material defaults.
  • A popup's unmount is a dismissal only when its overlay entry is settled.
  • menubar/bar.py imports nuiitivet.material. The slot imports it at its first build. No other module under menubar/ imports material.

docs.text: On macOS the model is installed as the application's main menu.

    focus -- "windows · _main_window · title" --> app
    focus -- "NSMenuBridge(controller, app_name) · install(model) · uninstall()" --> nsmenu
    focus -- "schedule_once(apply, 0)" --> clock
    nsmenu -- "NSMenuBuilder(controller.activate) · new_menu(title, entries) · dispose()" --> builder
    nsmenu -- "setMainMenu_(main_menu)" --> appkit
    builder -- "NSMenuItem · setTitle_ · setEnabled_ · setState_ · key equivalents" --> appkit
    builder -- "label, enabled, checked subscriptions · key_equivalent(shortcut)" --> entry
    builder -- "schedule_once(apply, 0)" --> clock
    appkit -- "nuiitivetMenuAction_(sender)" --> builder
    builder -- "activate(entry)" --> controller

docs.title: The bar follows the windows
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as controller.py
    participant F as focus.py
    participant K as observable/runtime.py
    participant N as nsmenu.py

    W->>F: window_created(window), the backend window is up
    F->>F: apply, at once
    W->>F: focus_changed(window, active=True), model_changed, or window_closed
    F->>K: schedule_once(apply, 0), once per burst
    K->>F: apply
    F->>F: the owner: the focused window with a menu, else the main window with one
    alt the owner and the model are the installed ones
        Note over F: nothing
    else another owner
        F->>N: NSMenuBridge(owner's controller, app_name).install(model)
        F->>N: old.uninstall()
    else the same owner, a replaced model
        F->>N: install(model), the same bridge
    end

docs.title: A property changes
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant E as menus/model.py
    participant B as menus/nsmenu.py
    participant K as observable/runtime.py
    participant A as AppKit

    E->>B: a label, enabled or checked Observable fires, any thread
    B->>K: schedule_once(apply, 0)
    K->>B: apply, on the UI thread
    B->>A: setTitle_ · setEnabled_ · setState_

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• One coordinator and one bridge per app.
  • The bar shows the focused window's model. The main window's model stands in for a window with menu=None.
  • The Cocoa imports happen lazily, on macOS only. plan_menus and key_equivalent import on every platform.
  • AppKit is touched on the UI thread only.

docs.title: Modifier
docs.text: A modifier wraps a widget to add a capability or a visual effect.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Four groups of modules take part, with the app at their edge.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    chain[The Chain]
    paint[The Paint Modifiers]
    interaction[The Interaction Modifiers]
    composed[The Composed Modifiers]
    app[the app]

    app -- "widget.modifier(a | b)" --> chain

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A modifier never changes layout.
  • A chain of paint modifiers is one node in the tree. A chain of interaction modifiers is one node in the tree.

docs.title: The Chain
docs.text: A ModifierElement turns a widget into a widget. A Modifier is a list of them.

docs.text:
flowchart LR
    modifier[widgeting/modifier.py]
    widget[widgeting/widget.py]
    elements[the modifier modules]
    app[the app]

docs.text: • An element decides for itself whether to wrap the widget or to merge into it.

• A paint modifier applied to a Box sets the property on that box. Applied to a ModifierBox, it rebuilds the box with the property merged. Applied to any other widget, it wraps the widget in a new ModifierBox.
  • A ModifierBox forwards a back event to its child.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• visible(False) keeps the widget mounted.
  • Input is blocked for the whole exit transition.
  • visible is opacity, passthrough_pointer and block_focus_traversal composed.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: A Navigator holds a stack of screens and paints the top one. Overlay is built on the same kernel (OVERLAY.md).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Four groups of modules take part: the window that owns the root navigator, the navigator package, the transition kernel both stacks stand on, and the Material layer that subclasses the navigator. The overlay, the reload snapshot, the will_pop modifier and a ViewModel stand at their edges.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    window[The Window]
    navigation[The Navigator]
    kernel[The Kernel]
    material[The Material Layer]
    overlay[overlay/overlay.py]
    snapshot[dev/navigation_snapshot.py]
    willpop[modifiers/will_pop.py]
    vm[a ViewModel]

    window -- "the root navigator · request_back" --> navigation
    window -- "async_request_close_topmost · occluding_content_widget" --> overlay
    navigation -- "StackRuntime · TransitionEngine · TransitionSpec" --> kernel
    overlay -- "StackRuntime" --> kernel
    material -- "subclasses, with its composer and default spec" --> navigation
    snapshot -- "snapshot_stack · restore_stack" --> navigation
    navigation -- "handle_back_event" --> willpop
    vm -- "NavigatorProtocol" --> navigation
Module Role The Window holds the root navigator and routes a back action The Navigator keeps the stack of routes, resolves a push, paints the top, absorbs back requests The Kernel tracks when an element enters, stays and exits a stack; drives the progress of a transition The Material Layer subclasses the navigator with the Material default and composer overlay/overlay.py the layers above the screen, offered a back action first (OVERLAY.md) dev/navigation_snapshot.py saves the route log before a reload and replays it after (HOT_RELOAD.md) modifiers/will_pop.py lets a screen refuse to be popped (MODIFIER.md) a ViewModel app code that pushes and pops through NavigatorProtocol

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• navigation and overlay import neither the other. Both import transition.
  • A screen enters the tree only as the widget of a route.

docs.title: The Window
docs.text: The window holds the root navigator and routes a back action.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    content[the content factory]
    window[Window]
    navigator[Navigator]
    overlay[Overlay]

    content -- "a Navigator, or a plain widget" --> window
    window -- "Navigator(widget) for a plain root · request_back()" --> navigator
    window -- "has_entries · async_request_close_topmost · occluding_content_widget" --> overlay
Module Role the content factory the window's content, returning the root Window holds the root navigator, wraps a plain root in the implicit one (MaterialApp overrides the wrap), offers a back action to the overlay and then the navigator Navigator the stack of screens (The Navigator) Overlay the layers above the screen (OVERLAY.md)

docs.title: A back action
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Window
    participant O as Overlay
    participant N as Navigator

    W->>O: has_entries()
    alt an entry is open
        W->>O: async_request_close_topmost()
        alt an entry closed
            O-->>W: handled
        else nothing closed, an entry still occludes
            Note over W: stops here
        else nothing closed, nothing occludes (a pass-through entry)
            W->>N: request_back()
            N-->>W: handled, or False at the root route
        end
    else no entry
        W->>N: request_back()
        N-->>W: handled, or False at the root route
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A window owns one root navigator. A plain widget given as the content is wrapped in one.
  • A back action never reaches past an occluding overlay entry, an entry animating out included. A pass-through entry blocks nothing.
  • The window handles one request per input.

docs.title: The Navigator
docs.text: The navigator keeps routes on a stack from the kernel, resolves a push to a route, paints through a layer composer, and absorbs back requests.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    navigator[Navigator]
    route[Route]
    stack["StackRuntime[Route]"]
    engine[TransitionEngine]
    composer[NavigationLayerComposer]
    proto[NavigatorProtocol]
    routes[the intent table]
    screen[the outgoing screen]
    snapshot[dev/navigation_snapshot.py]

    navigator -- "Route(widget, transition)" --> route
    navigator -- "push · mark_active · mark_exiting · complete_exit" --> stack
    navigator -- "start(progress, motion, on_complete)" --> engine
    navigator -- "paint_static · paint_transition" --> composer
    navigator -- "the factory for an intent's type" --> routes
    navigator -- "handle_back_event(), before a pop" --> screen
    navigator -. "implements" .-> proto
    snapshot -- "snapshot_stack · restore_stack" --> navigator
Module Role Navigator push turns a widget or an intent into a route and starts the enter transition; pop and request_back take one route off, absorbing requests during a transition; of finds the navigator a widget drives; paint draws the top route or a transition frame; _restore_log keeps a descriptor per push Route a screen and the transition it moves with; disposing it unmounts the screen StackRuntime[Route] the stack from the kernel (The Kernel) TransitionEngine drives the progress of a transition (The Kernel) NavigationLayerComposer the paint of a static screen and of a transition frame NavigatorProtocol the three methods a ViewModel is typed against the intent table Navigator.routes: an intent type to the factory that builds its screen, or its screen and transition the outgoing screen asked before a pop; the question is forwarded down its built tree to a will_pop modifier dev/navigation_snapshot.py the reload's read and replay of the log (HOT_RELOAD.md)

docs.title: A screen is pushed and popped
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant N as Navigator
    participant S as StackRuntime
    participant E as TransitionEngine
    participant C as layer composer
    participant R as the new Route

    N->>S: push(B), mark_active(B)
    N->>E: start(0 → 1, motion: B.enter)
    loop each frame
        E->>N: progress
        N->>C: paint_transition(from A via A.exit_, to B via B.enter)
    end
    E->>N: complete
    Note over N,C: paint_static(B) from here
    N->>N: pop()
    N->>S: mark_exiting(B)
    N->>E: start(1 → 0, motion: B.exit_back)
    loop each frame
        E->>N: progress
        N->>C: paint_transition(from B via B.exit_back, to A via A.enter_back)
    end
    E->>N: complete
    N->>S: complete_exit(B)
    S->>R: dispose() → unmount

docs.title: A back request reaches the navigator
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Window
    participant N as Navigator
    participant E as TransitionEngine
    participant S as the outgoing screen

    W->>N: request_back()
    alt a pop is in flight
        N->>N: pending_pop_requests += 1
        N->>E: finish the running pop at once
        loop while pending_pop_requests > 0
            N->>N: _pop_once(skip_animation = not the last)
        end
    else a push is in flight
        N->>E: finish the push at once
        N->>N: _pop_once()
    else idle
        N->>N: _pop_once()
    end
    Note over N,S: inside each _pop_once
    N->>S: handle_back_event() down to will_pop
    alt the screen refuses
        S-->>N: False
        N->>N: pending_pop_requests = 0
    else the screen allows
        S-->>N: True
        N->>E: start the pop
    end

docs.title: The stack is restored after a reload
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as dev/controller.py
    participant S as dev/navigation_snapshot.py
    participant Old as the navigator before the reload
    participant New as the navigator after the reload

    C->>S: snapshot_navigation()
    S->>Old: snapshot_stack()
    Old-->>S: the restore log, bottom to top
    C->>C: rebuild the content from the window's factory
    C->>S: restore_navigation(log)
    S->>New: restore_stack(log)
    loop each entry
        alt an intent still registered
            New->>New: resolve it, push the route without animation
        else a widget push, or an intent no longer registered
            Note over New: replay stops, the screens above are lost
        end
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A screen's transition is held by its route until the route is disposed.
  • A screen pushed with no transition moves with the navigator's default.
  • Outside a transition only the top route is painted. The routes beneath stay mounted.
  • Each screen of a transition is painted through its own spec.
  • The restore log replays intent pushes only.
  • Queued pops run without animation, except the last.
  • No pop starts against the outgoing screen's refusal. A refusal discards the queue.
  • A refused pop still counts as handled.

docs.title: The Kernel
docs.text: The kernel tracks when an element enters, stays and exits a stack, and drives the progress of a transition. It knows nothing of screens or layers.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    navigator[Navigator]
    overlay[Overlay]
    stack[StackRuntime]
    entry[StackEntry]
    engine[TransitionEngine]
    handle[TransitionHandle]
    spec[TransitionSpec]
    phase[TransitionPhase]
    element[an element]

    navigator & overlay -- "push · mark_active · mark_exiting · complete_exit" --> stack
    navigator -- "start(start, target, apply, on_complete, motion)" --> engine
    stack -- "holds" --> entry -- "element · lifecycle" --> element
    stack -- "dispose() on complete_exit" --> element
    engine -- "returns" --> handle
    navigator -- "cancel()" --> handle
    spec -- "the motion of a phase: enter · exit_ · enter_back · exit_back" --> phase
Module Role Navigator, Overlay the two stacks built on the kernel (The Navigator, OVERLAY.md) StackRuntime the ordered elements and their lifecycle: entering, active, exiting, disposed StackEntry one element with its lifecycle state TransitionEngine animates one progress from start to target and reports completion TransitionHandle cancels a running transition TransitionSpec, EmptyTransitionSpec the four motions of a screen; the spec that moves nothing TransitionPhase which of the four motions a frame is in an element a Route, or an overlay layer; anything with dispose()

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The stack holds any element with a dispose(). It disposes an element when its exit completes.
  • The engine drives one progress per transition and reports completion once.

docs.title: The Material Layer
docs.text: The Material navigator subclasses Navigator with its own composer and its own default.

docs.text:
flowchart LR
    app["MaterialApp._build_default_navigator"]
    matnav[MaterialNavigator]
    matcomposer[MaterialNavigationLayerComposer]
    specs["MaterialTransitions.page()"]
