docs.text:
• MaterialNavigator adds no navigation API.
  • The default transition is a subclass hook. Navigator defaults to the empty spec; MaterialNavigator to the page transition.

docs.title: Observable
docs.text: An Observable is a value that notifies when it changes. A domain model, a service or a widget holds one. Every node of the graph is built on one shared base. Two kinds of node stand on it: a derivation of other nodes, and a wrapper that reshapes what its source emits. A widget joins the graph through its value cell. The thread the graph runs on is defined in CONCURRENCY_MODEL.md.

docs.title: What Every Observable Shares
docs.text: The shared base carries the held value, the notify loop, the batch, the marshalling of a worker's write onto the UI thread, and the containment of a callback that raises. The Structure is the whole page: the shared modules, and the three subjects below as groups.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    handler["UI handler (inside batch)"]
    worker[worker thread]
    subgraph base[the shared base]
        value[_ObservableValue]
        protocols["ObservableProtocol · Disposable"]
        notify["notify_all()"]
        batching[BatchContext]
        contexts["_batch_context · _tracking_context"]
        clock[the installed clock]
        threading["is_ui_thread()"]
        input[widget_input.py]
    end
    deriving[Deriving Operators]
    wrapping[Wrapping Operators]
    cell[The Value Cell]

    handler -- ".value = …" --> value
    worker -- ".value = …" --> value
    input -- "batch() around a dispatch" --> batching
    value -- "notify_all(subscribers, current)" --> notify
    value -- "schedule_once(flush, 0) off the UI thread" --> clock
    value -- "is_ui_thread()" --> threading
    value -- "record_change" --> batching
    batching -- "get · set" --> contexts
    deriving -- "subscribe to the sources · record_computed · _tracking_context" --> base
    wrapping -- "subscribe to the source · schedule_once · notify_all" --> base
    cell -- "isinstance(ObservableProtocol) · subscribe" --> base
Module Role _ObservableValue the mutable value node: compares, decides whether a write is marshalled, notifies (observable/value.py) ObservableProtocol, Disposable the read-only and writable protocols, the subscription handle, the mark for the graph's own edges (observable/protocols.py) notify_all() the one loop that delivers a value to every subscriber, surviving one that raises (observable/_notify.py) BatchContext records the dirty values and the queued derivations, flushes at the outermost exit (observable/batching.py) _batch_context, _tracking_context the two contextvars: the current batch, the tracking derivation (observable/contexts.py) the installed clock carries every timer and every marshalled notification to the UI thread (observable/runtime.py) is_ui_thread() the one definition of the UI thread (runtime/threading.py) widget_input.py dispatches pointer, key and focus events, each inside a batch (widgeting/) Deriving Operators compute a value from other nodes and hold no state Wrapping Operators stay subscribed to a source and reshape what it emits The Value Cell the cell an input widget keeps its value in, and the bindings that repaint it

docs.title: A write from a worker thread
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as worker thread
    participant V as _ObservableValue
    participant C as installed clock
    participant U as UI thread
    participant S as subscribers

    W->>V: .value = v
    alt dispatch and not is_ui_thread()
        V->>V: hold v as the pending value
        V->>C: schedule_once(flush, 0)
        C->>U: next tick
        U->>V: flush the newest pending value
        V->>S: notify_all
    else on the UI thread, or dispatch=False
        V->>S: notify_all
    end

docs.title: A handler inside a batch
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant I as widget_input.py
    participant H as handler
    participant V as _ObservableValue
    participant B as BatchContext
    participant D as ComputedObservable
    participant S as subscribers

    I->>B: enter batch()
    I->>H: dispatch the event
    H->>V: .value = v
    V->>S: notify_all (direct subscribers)
    V->>D: the dependency edge fires
    D->>B: record_computed, no recompute
    V->>B: record_change
    H->>V: .value = w
    Note over V,B: the same steps, the same entries
    I->>B: exit the outermost batch
    B->>D: recompute once
    D->>S: notify_all

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A value node and a derivation compare the new value with the held one before notifying. A wrapper does not.
  • A write from a thread other than the UI thread is marshalled onto the UI thread. One flush per tick carries the newest value.
  • A write on the UI thread applies inline.
  • dispatch=False keeps a node's notification synchronous on the writing thread. Every intermediate value is delivered.
  • A derivation, a predicate or a fold runs on the thread that triggered it.
  • batch() nests. Each derivation a batch reaches recomputes once, at the outermost exit. A batch exited off the UI thread marshals that flush when any dirty value dispatches.
  • Pointer, key and focus dispatch run inside batch().
  • _ObservableValue, ComputedObservable and SourceSubscribingObservable each define the full operator set.
  • A derivation, a predicate or a fold that raises is contained where it runs. The node keeps the value it held. Nothing is emitted. The failure is logged once.
  • A subscriber that raises is contained in the notify loop. The subscribers after it are still notified. The value is re-read per subscriber.
  • The graph's own edges carry mark_internal_subscription. An exception on one of them re-raises. The leak check in testing/_leaks.py exempts them.

docs.title: Deriving Operators
docs.text: map, combine and compute answer "what is .value now" with a function of their sources. They hold no state of their own.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    map["map()"]
    builder[CombineBuilder]
    computed[ComputedObservable]
    tracking[(_tracking_context)]
    sources[(the source nodes)]

    map -- "ComputedObservable(fn, dispatch)" --> computed
    builder -- "compute(fn)" --> computed
    computed -- "set during the function" --> tracking
    tracking -- "every .value read" --> computed
    computed -- "subscribe, weakly, with the internal mark" --> sources
Module Role map() builds a ComputedObservable over one source; defined on every kind of node CombineBuilder collects several sources for one compute(fn) ComputedObservable runs the function under the tracking context, re-arms its edges, stores the result _tracking_context the derivation currently running, so a read can register itself the source nodes whatever the function reads

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The .value reads during the function are the dependencies. They are collected anew on every run, whether the run raised or not.
  • An edge from a source to a derivation holds the derivation weakly.
  • map carries its source's dispatch into the derivation it builds.

docs.title: Wrapping Operators
docs.text: debounce, throttle, filter, switch_map and scan stay subscribed to their source until they are disposed. The first three reshape when or whether a source's value is republished. The last two publish values of their own.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    source[(the source node)]
    base["SourceSubscribingObservable[TIn, TOut]"]
    shaping["ShapingObservable[T]"]
    debounce[DebouncedObservable]
    throttle[ThrottledObservable]
    filter[FilteredObservable]
    switch[SwitchMappedObservable]
    scan[ScannedObservable]
    clock[installed clock]
    thread[daemon thread]
    task[spawn_task]

    base -- "subscribe, weakly" --> source
    shaping -- "is a" --> base
    debounce & throttle & filter -- "is a" --> shaping
    switch & scan -- "is a" --> base
    debounce & throttle -- "schedule_once · unschedule" --> clock
    switch -- "a plain fn" --> thread
    switch -- "a coroutine fn" --> task
    thread & task -- "_deliver(result, token)" --> switch
    switch -- "schedule_once(_flush, 0)" --> clock
Module Role SourceSubscribingObservable the base of every wrapper: the weak edge to the source, the held value, the teardown ShapingObservable the base of the wrappers whose output type is the input type DebouncedObservable, ThrottledObservable republish on the trailing edge, or on the leading edge, of a time window FilteredObservable republishes only the values the predicate passes SwitchMappedObservable, CancelToken runs fn per change and publishes only the newest run's result ScannedObservable folds every emission into an accumulator the daemon thread runs a plain fn off the UI thread spawn_task runs a coroutine fn as a task on the event loop the installed clock carries a timer or a marshalled result to the UI thread the source node the node a wrapper subscribes to

docs.title: A switch_map run superseded by the next change
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Src as source
    participant SM as SwitchMappedObservable
    participant R1 as run 1 (thread or task)
    participant R2 as run 2 (thread or task)
    participant C as installed clock
    participant S as subscribers

    Src->>SM: value a
    SM->>R1: fn(a), token 1
    Src->>SM: value b
    SM->>SM: supersede token 1, drop its stage, cancel its task
    SM->>R2: fn(b), token 2
    R1-->>SM: _deliver(result, token 1)
    Note over SM: token 1 is not the current one: dropped
    R2->>SM: _deliver(result, token 2)
    SM->>SM: stage the result under the lock
    SM->>C: schedule_once(_flush, 0)
    C->>SM: _flush on the UI thread
    SM->>S: notify_all, outside the lock

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A wrapper subscribes to its source through a weak reference to itself.
  • A wrapper is kept alive by its holder, by the Disposable its subscribe() returned, or by a timer it armed until the timer fires.
  • dispose() drops the source subscription. It unschedules every callback the wrapper may have armed.
  • .value is the value the wrapper last emitted. Before the first emission it is the seed. The value is stored before the subscribers are notified.
  • .value registers the wrapper with the tracking context, never its source. The wrapper's own reads, and the callbacks it runs, are untracked.
  • A wrapper has no dispatch flag. A wrapper that re-publishes on its source's notification emits on that thread. A wrapper that emits from a timer or a run emits through the installed clock.
  • The clock finds the callback to unschedule by equality.
  • debounce and throttle seed from the source's construction-time value. Each holds only the latest pending value.
  • filter tests the source's construction-time value against the predicate.
  • switch_map and scan seed from initial, reading nothing from the source. switch_map starts no run at construction.
  • A plain switch_map function runs on a thread of its own. A coroutine function runs as a task on the event loop.
  • A superseded switch_map result never lands. dispose() supersedes the run in flight.
  • scan emits once per emission in.

docs.title: An entry is shown and closed
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as the app
    participant O as overlay.py
    participant R as transition/stack.py
    participant E as transition/engine.py
    participant L as layout/stack.py

    A->>O: show(content, ...)
    O->>R: push(layer)
    O->>L: add_child(layer widget)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Paint order is insertion order.
  • An entry's widget mounts once, when shown. It unmounts once, when its entry leaves the stack. The other layers are untouched by a show or a close.
  • Overlay.of searches the ancestors for the calling class first, then falls back to the window's overlay.
  • An entry stays open until its exit transition finishes.
  • The keyboard side of passthrough is read through occluding_content_widget(), the content of the topmost layer shown with passthrough=False.
  • A window takes its overlay as it takes its content. An instance keeps the window hot-reload inert. A factory is re-invoked on a reload.

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as the app
    participant H as overlay_handle.py
    participant O as overlay.py
    participant P as modifiers/will_pop.py

    A->>H: await handle
    H->>O: _future_for_entry(entry)

docs.title: A reload carries an entry
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as dev/overlay_snapshot.py
    participant Old as the old overlay.py
    participant New as the new overlay.py

    S->>Old: snapshot_stack()
    Old->>Old: mark the entries shown from an intent as carried
    Old-->>S: the records, intent and replay and handle
    Note over Old: unmount, the carried entries complete nothing
    S->>New: restore_stack(records)

        New->>Old: take the entry's future
        New->>New: the old handle now points at the new entry
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• An await never hangs. An entry removed without a close completes with DISPOSED, unless a snapshot carried it to the rebuilt overlay.
  • A result is settled once. A settled result survives the entry's removal until the handle reads it.
  • OverlayAware content holds its handle before its first build.
  • An entry shown from an intent survives a reload with its handle. One shown from a widget does not.
  • A refusal from will_pop keeps the entry open.
  • Unmounting the overlay removes every entry at once, without exit transitions.

docs.text: A frame's paint cost is the Python walk of the widget tree. Three caches skip part of that walk: one widget's own visuals, the whole frame, and the rows of a scroll viewport.

    participant V as scroll_viewport.py
    participant U as layout_utils.py
    participant K as widget_kernel.py
    participant T as the widget tree

    V->>U: content.paint(canvas, x, y - offset, w, h), the hint set
    alt the canvas is skewed or rotated
        U->>T: paint(canvas, x, y, w, h), every row
    else
        loop each row
            alt outside the clip
                U->>K: _replay_picture = None
            else clean, with a picture for this size and scale

            else changed, or no picture

                else
                    U->>T: paint(recorder, x, y, w, h), under the canvas matrix
                    U->>K: _replay_picture, _replay_origin, _replay_key
                    U->>U: drawPicture
                end
            end
        end
    end

• A row is replayed only when every widget in it declares each of its draw methods with replay_safe.

  • A handled pointer event marks the widget that handled it.
  • A scroll marks nothing below the viewport.
  • A declared widget takes the position its input needs from layout, never from its last paint.
  • The pictures held are those of the rows on screen.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Every core symbol is reachable from the Material root.
  • A function sits flat on the root only as DSL vocabulary. Configuration and OS services live on a namespace class.

docs.text: • A core name the Material root overrides resolves to the Material class.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A namespace class is never instantiated. The implementation stays in its subsystem.
  • The class name is a plural or collective noun for the subsystem or the service. A method drops the words the class name carries.

docs.title: Rendering Pipeline
docs.text: A window draws a frame on demand.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Four groups of modules take part.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    loop[The Loop]
    frame[The Frame]
    measure[The Measure]
    painter[The Child Painter]
    widget[widgeting/widget.py]
    clock[observable/runtime.py]

    widget -- "invalidate() · mark_needs_layout()" --> frame
    frame -- "request_draw(immediate)" --> loop
    loop -- "_render_frame(dt), each open window" --> frame
    loop -- "the tick" --> clock
    clock -- "the tick" --> widget
    frame -- "root.layout(w, h) · root.paint(canvas, 0, 0, w, h)" --> measure
    measure -- "layout_child_if_needed · paint_laid_out_children" --> painter
Module Role The Loop decides each iteration whether a frame is drawn The Frame one window's frame, from the queues to the flip The Measure the caches a layout pass reads The Child Painter lays a container's children out and paints them widgeting/widget.py invalidate, the one request for a frame (WIDGET_ARCHITECTURE.md) observable/runtime.py the clock animations tick on (ANIMATION_SYSTEM.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A frame is drawn only when something invalidated.
  • A flip follows a full repaint of the back buffer.
  • layout() issues no draw command. layout() writes no Observable. A measured result reaches an Observable through the size-change queue.
  • preferred_size() has no side effect. On a mounted composable it never calls build().

docs.title: The Loop
docs.text: ResponsiveEventLoop wakes for OS events, the clock and a pending frame.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    loop[backends/pyglet/event_loop.py]
    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    clock[observable/runtime.py]
    pyglet[pyglet]

    runner -- "ResponsiveEventLoop(draw, fps, keep_running_without_windows) · run()" --> loop
    runner -- "invalidate(), on resize" --> window
    window -- "request_draw(immediate)" --> loop
    loop -- "_render_frame(dt), each open window" --> window
    loop -- "update_time() · call_scheduled_functions(dt) · get_sleep_time()" --> clock
    loop -- "platform_event_loop.step(timeout) · set_timer(_blocking_timer, timeout)" --> pyglet
    pyglet -- "idle(), from the OS drag loop" --> loop
    pyglet -- "on_resize" --> runner
Module Role backends/pyglet/event_loop.py decides whether a frame is drawn this iteration. Decides how long to sleep backends/pyglet/runner.py builds the loop with the draw callback; the OS event handlers (APP_WINDOW.md) runtime/window.py requests a frame, draws one (The Frame) observable/runtime.py the clock the loop ticks (OBSERVABLE.md) pyglet the platform event loop

docs.title: A frame is requested and drawn
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant L as backends/pyglet/event_loop.py
    participant P as pyglet

    W->>L: request_draw(immediate)
    L->>L: _draw_pending = True
    loop each iteration
        L->>P: step(timeout)
        L->>L: tick the clock
        alt _draw_pending, and no cadence or the deadline passed
            L->>L: _draw_pending = False
            L->>W: _render_frame(dt), each open window
        end
        L->>L: _compute_sleep_timeout(): the deadline when a frame is pending, else the clock's next due time
    end

docs.title: The OS owns the loop during a drag
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant OS as the OS drag loop
    participant P as pyglet
    participant R as backends/pyglet/runner.py
    participant L as backends/pyglet/event_loop.py
    participant W as runtime/window.py

    Note over L: blocked inside step() until the mouse is released
    OS->>P: the window resized
    P->>R: on_resize
    R->>W: invalidate()
    P->>L: idle()
    L->>L: tick the clock, _should_draw(now)
    L->>W: _render_frame(dt), when a frame is pending
    L-->>P: the sleep timeout, re-arming the Win32 timer

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• With nothing pending the loop draws nothing. It does not wake for a cadence deadline.
  • A cadence throttles a pending frame and never produces one.
  • A frame served from the OS drag loop passes the same gate as one from the main loop.

docs.title: The Frame
docs.text: _render_frame draws one window.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    window[runtime/window.py]
    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]
    gpu[backends/pyglet/gpu_frame.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    pyglet[pyglet]

    window -- "switch_to() · dispatch_event(on_draw) · flip()" --> pyglet
    pyglet -- "on_draw" --> runner
    runner -- "draw_gpu_frame(win, gr_context, GL, skia)" --> gpu
    runner -- "_render_display_frame(scale), the raster path" --> window
    gpu & window -- "root.layout(w, h) · clear_needs_layout() · root.paint(canvas, 0, 0, w, h)" --> kernel
Module Role runtime/window.py draws a window's frame; renders the raster path's image backends/pyglet/runner.py on_draw: the GPU path, falling back to the raster path backends/pyglet/gpu_frame.py paints the tree into the GL framebuffer, or re-blits the cached frame (PAINT_CACHE.md) widgeting/widget_kernel.py the root's layout and paint pyglet the window and its back buffer

docs.title: A window draws a frame
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant P as pyglet
    participant R as backends/pyglet/runner.py
    participant G as backends/pyglet/gpu_frame.py
    participant K as widget_kernel.py

    W->>W: _render_frame(dt)
    Note over W: the queues are flushed, in the order GEOMETRY.md draws
    W->>P: switch_to(), dispatch_event(on_draw)
    P->>R: on_draw
    R->>G: draw_gpu_frame(win, ...)
    alt the tree is clean and the cache fits
        G->>G: re-blit the cached frame
    else
        G->>K: root.layout(w, h), when needs_layout or the size changed
        G->>K: root.paint(canvas, 0, 0, w, h)
    end
    W->>P: flip()

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Layout runs to completion before the first draw command.
  • The GPU path and the raster path lay out and paint the same tree with the same calls.

docs.title: The Measure
docs.text: Three caches keep a layout pass proportional to what changed.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    measure[layout/measure.py]
    engine[layout/layout_engine.py]
    sizing[rendering/sizing.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    containers[the containers]

    containers -- "preferred_size(widget, max_w, max_h)" --> measure
    measure -- "_measure_cache · preferred_size(max_w, max_h)" --> kernel
    containers -- "preferred_size · compute_inner_rect · compute_child_placement · resolve_child_geometry" --> engine
    engine -- "_layout_cache_token · padding" --> kernel
    kernel -- "parse_sizing(value)" --> sizing
Module Role layout/measure.py remembers a widget's measurement per constraint pair, a short list per widget layout/layout_engine.py remembers a container's preferred size, inner rect and child placement, keyed on padding, border and the tokens rendering/sizing.py parses a sizing literal once widgeting/widget_kernel.py holds the measure cache slot and the layout cache token; mark_needs_layout drops them up the tree the containers Row, Column, Container and the others that measure their children (LAYOUT.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Shrinking a maximum constraint down to the measured result leaves the result unchanged. The measure cache answers a shrunk constraint from the entry it still fits.
  • A change routed through mark_needs_layout re-measures the dirtied path only.

docs.title: The Child Painter
docs.text: layout_utils lays a container's children out and paints them at their rects.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    utils[layout/layout_utils.py]
    kernel[widgeting/widget_kernel.py]
    containers[the containers]
    skia[rendering/skia/geometry.py]

    containers -- "layout_child_if_needed(child, w, h) · paint_laid_out_children(container, canvas, x, y, w, h)" --> utils
    utils -- "needs_layout · layout_rect · layout(w, h) · paint(canvas, x, y, w, h)" --> kernel
    utils -- "paint_outsets() · set_last_rect(x, y, w, h) · _paint_inside_clip" --> kernel
    utils -- "local_clip_bounds(canvas)" --> skia
Module Role layout/layout_utils.py lays a child out unless it is clean at the same size; paints the children, skipping those beyond the clip and its slack band; tells a child inside the clip so widgeting/widget_kernel.py layout, paint, last_rect; the paint hints a parent sets for the paint that follows the containers the multi-child containers (LAYOUT.md) rendering/skia/geometry.py reads the canvas clip

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A clean child laid out again at the same size is skipped.
  • A child whose rect plus outsets lies outside the clip and its slack band is not painted. It still receives its last_rect.
  • Without a readable clip every child is painted.
  • A wrapper passes the inside-clip hint only while it neither narrows the clip nor moves its child. A hint covers one paint.

docs.title: Style and Theme
docs.text: A widget's look is a style, one dataclass per widget. A theme supplies the colours a style names. A design system may put another default style in the theme. How a widget reads the theme is in THEME_CONSUMPTION.md.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three groups of modules take part.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    theme[The Theme]
    material[The Material Theme]
    styles[The Styles]
    widgets[the Material widgets]
    generic[the generic widgets]
    app[the app]

    app -- "MaterialThemeFactory.from_seed(seed, mode, variant, contrast_level, form_factor)" --> material
    app -- "App(theme=...) · set_theme(theme)" --> theme
    material -- "Theme(mode, extensions, name) · ThemeExtension" --> theme
    widgets -- "Theme.of(self) · theme.extension(MaterialThemeData)" --> theme
    widgets -- "Style.from_theme(theme) · style.copy_with(...) · ColorSpec fields" --> styles
    styles -- "resolve_color_to_rgba(spec, theme)" --> theme
    generic -- "theme.extension(ScrollbarThemeData) · theme.extension(MenuBarThemeData)" --> theme

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Everything design-specific lives in a ThemeExtension.
  • A generic widget never reads a Material colour role.
  • The app-wide palette lives in a ThemeExtension. A per-instance override lives in the nullable ColorSpec fields of the widget's style. The shape lives in the style.

docs.text: Theme is the container every design system fills.

docs.text:
• A colour token resolves at paint, against the theme current then.
  • A theme holds at most one extension per type.
  • The manager notifies one owner.

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as the Material widgets
    participant S as material/styles/

docs.text:
• An empty slot falls through to one shared frozen preset.
  • A style keeps the MD3 baseline numbers under every form factor. The widget applies the form factor where it measures and paints.
  • A style's own density wins over the theme's step.

docs.text: Each widget has its own style class.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A style is frozen. A variation is a copy_with, never a mutation.
  • No style class inherits from another.
  • Every style class with presets has default().

docs.title: Text Editing
docs.text: A text field keeps its state in an immutable value. Typed text, key shortcuts and the OS input method all turn one value into the next.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Four groups of modules take part, with the app and the OS input method at their edges.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    value[The Value]
    editor[The Editor]
    dispatch[The Dispatch]
    ime[The IME]
    app[the app]
    os[the OS input method]

    app -- "TextField(value, on_change, on_submit, input_filter) · TextField.multiline(...)" --> editor
    editor -- "insert_text · compose_text · end_composition · apply_motion · apply_shortcut · apply(old, new)" --> value
    dispatch -- "on_text · on_key · on_text_motion · on_ime_composition · on_ime_commit" --> editor
    os -- "a composition update · where is the caret" --> ime
    ime -- "on_ime_composition(text, start, length)" --> dispatch
    editor -- "set_cursor_source(rect_fn)" --> ime
Module Role The Value the immutable editing value and the pure functions that produce the next one The Editor the widget that holds the value, mirrors its text to the app and draws it The Dispatch routes typed text, motions and compositions to the focused field The IME the patch on each platform window and the caret the OS asks for the app binds a str observable and the callbacks the OS input method composes text inline and places its candidates at the caret

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Typed text and key presses arrive on two routes. A field inserts characters from on_text. It claims keys on on_key.
  • The IME is reached by patching the platform window, never through the backend's own text input.

docs.title: The Value
docs.text: TextEditingValue is a snapshot of a field: the text, the selection and the range the IME is still converting.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The composing range is part of the text until the IME commits.
  • A filter runs on typing, a paste and an IME commit. It runs on no deletion and on no value the app assigns.

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant I as widgets/interaction.py
    participant E as editable_text.py
    participant V as text_editing.py
    participant O as observable/
    participant A as the app

    I->>E: on_text(text)
    E->>V: insert_text(value, text, filter)
    V-->>E: the new value, filtered
    E->>E: _update_value(new)
    alt composing, or the text equals the last announced
        Note over E: no announcement
    else
        E->>O: obs.value = text
        O->>E: _on_external_change(text), equal, returns
        E->>A: on_change(text)
    end

docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as the app
    participant O as observable/
    participant E as editable_text.py

    A->>O: obs.value = "ABC"
    O->>E: _on_external_change("ABC")
    E->>E: the caret kept, clamped into the new text
    E->>A: on_change("ABC")

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• on_change fires for every text change, from the user or from the app. The write-back fires for the user's edits only.
  • Nothing is announced while a composition is active. Ending the composition announces the text, changed or not.
  • The write-back loop ends on equality.
  • A field without on_submit declines Enter.
  • An Enter that confirms an IME composition is not a submit.

docs.title: The Dispatch
docs.text: The window routes text, motions and compositions to the focused node. The node bubbles them up its chain.

docs.title: Structure

    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    interaction[widgets/interaction.py]
    editor[widgets/editable_text.py]
    shortcuts[input/shortcut.py]

    runner -- "_dispatch_text(text) · _dispatch_text_motion(motion, select) · _dispatch_ime_composition(text, start, length) · _dispatch_key_press(key, mods) · _set_os_active(active)" --> window
    window -- "handle_text_event(text) · handle_text_motion_event · handle_ime_composition_event · handle_ime_commit_event() · handle_key_event · accepts_text_input" --> interaction
    interaction -- "on_text · on_text_motion · on_ime_composition · on_ime_commit · on_key" --> editor
    window -- "produces_text(key, modifier_keys)" --> shortcuts
Module Role backends/pyglet/runner.py the on_text, on_text_motion, on_ime_composition and activate handlers (APP_WINDOW.md) runtime/window.py hands each event to the focused node widgets/interaction.py FocusNode: the handlers and the bubbling to the parent node widgets/editable_text.py the field at the end of the chain (The Editor) input/shortcut.py the text guard of the shortcut tier (KEYBOARD_SHORTCUTS.md)

docs.title: The window loses the OS focus mid-composition
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as backends/pyglet/runner.py
    participant W as runtime/window.py
    participant I as widgets/interaction.py
    participant E as editable_text.py

    R->>W: _set_os_active(False)
    W->>I: handle_ime_commit_event()
    I->>E: on_ime_commit()
    E->>E: end_composition: the provisional text kept, the range cleared

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A window blocked by a modal child consumes a text event.
  • A key the focused chain can type reaches no shortcut.
  • A field holds no live composition while its window lacks the OS focus.

docs.title: The IME
docs.text: Each platform window is patched to intercept the input method before the OS handles it. The window's IMEManager answers where the caret is.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    manager[platform/ime.py]
    macos[backends/pyglet/ime/macos.py]
    windows[backends/pyglet/ime/windows.py]
    linux[backends/pyglet/ime/linux.py]
    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    editor[widgets/editable_text.py]
    os[the OS input method]

    runner -- "install_patch(pyglet_window, window) · discard_conversation(pyglet_window)" --> macos & windows & linux
    runner -- "update_window_info(x, y, w, h), on draw" --> manager
    window -- "IMEManager()" --> manager
    editor -- "set_cursor_source(rect_fn) · clear_cursor_source(rect_fn)" --> manager
    macos & windows & linux -- "cursor_rect" --> manager
    macos & windows & linux -- "on_ime_composition(text, start, length)" --> runner
    os -- "setMarkedText · WM_IME_COMPOSITION · PreeditDraw · the caret query" --> macos & windows & linux
Module Role platform/ime.py IMEManager: the window's position and the caret source backends/pyglet/ime/macos.py overrides setMarkedText:selectedRange:replacementRange: and firstRectForCharacterRange:actualRange: on the NSTextView through the Objective-C runtime backends/pyglet/ime/windows.py subclasses the window procedure for the composition messages backends/pyglet/ime/linux.py recreates the X input context with preedit callbacks backends/pyglet/runner.py installs the patch when the window is realised; drops the OS conversation on deactivate (APP_WINDOW.md) runtime/window.py owns the manager (APP_WINDOW.md) widgets/editable_text.py the focused field, the caret source (The Editor) the OS input method composes and asks for the caret

docs.title: The OS asks where the caret is
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant OS as the OS input method
    participant P as ime/macos.py, windows.py or linux.py
    participant M as platform/ime.py
    participant E as editable_text.py

    OS->>P: the caret query
    P->>M: cursor_rect
    M->>E: _ime_caret_rect(), the registered source
    E->>E: the caret's line and x from layout, the scroll settled
    E-->>M: the rect in window coordinates
    M-->>P: the rect plus the window's position
    P-->>OS: the rect in screen coordinates

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• One IMEManager per window.
  • The focused field is its window's caret source. It withdraws on unmount.
  • The caret rect is computed when the OS asks, from layout state. Nothing publishes it on paint.
  • A window that loses the OS focus drops its OS-side conversation.

docs.title: Theme Consumption
docs.text: How a widget reads the theme, and how a theme change reaches it. What a theme holds is in STYLE_THEME.md.

docs.title: What Every Reader Shares
docs.text: A reader is whatever unit the framework can invalidate.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    readers[the readers]
    provider[The Provider]
    lookup[The Lookup]
    dependency[The Dependency]
    color[rendering/skia/color.py]

    readers -- "Theme.of(self)" --> lookup
    lookup -- "theme_manager.current" --> provider
    lookup -- "register_theme_dependency · push_theme_reader · pop_theme_reader" --> dependency
    provider -- "invalidate_theme_readers(root)" --> dependency
    dependency -- "rebuild · mark_needs_layout · invalidate_paint_cache" --> readers
    readers -- "ThemeKept.get · theme_generation" --> dependency
    readers -- "shared_paint(color, stroke)" --> color
Module Role the readers the widgets that read the theme: in build(), at paint or measure, or through a kept value The Provider holds the current theme and fans a change out to every window The Lookup resolves Theme.of to the scope above the context, along the parent chain The Dependency marks a reader, finds the marks on a change, keeps a resolved value for a leaf rendering/skia/color.py hands out one paint per colour and stroke

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A widget obtains the theme only through Theme.of(context).
  • A widget with a build() reads in build(). A leaf reads in paint() or preferred_size().
  • A resolved value on a field is a cache of the read. It is applied again when the theme above the widget has moved.
  • No widget subscribes to the theme.
  • A ThemeKept holds colours, never a Skia paint. A paint is obtained from shared_paint by what it draws.

docs.title: The Provider
docs.text: The AppScope owns the ThemeManager. A theme change is one call that fans out to every window.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    app[App]
    mgr[ThemeManager]
    scope[AppScope]
    dep[theme/dependency.py]
    win[Window]

    app -- "set_theme(theme)" --> mgr -- "on_change(theme)" --> scope
    scope -- "theme_manager, owned" --> mgr
    scope -- "invalidate_theme_readers(window.root)" --> dep
    scope -- "_update_background_color() · invalidate()" --> win
Module Role App the one entry for a theme change, set_theme ThemeManager holds the current theme and the generation counter; notifies its one owner AppScope owns the manager; fans a change out to every open window theme/dependency.py invalidates the readers under a root (The Dependency) Window redraws a background drawn from a token, repaints

docs.title: A theme change reaches its readers
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as App
    participant M as ThemeManager
    participant S as AppScope
    participant D as dependency.py
    participant Rd as the marked readers
    participant W as each Window

    A->>M: set_theme(theme)
    M->>M: current = theme, generation += 1
    M->>S: on_change(theme)
    loop each open window
        S->>D: invalidate_theme_readers(window.root)
        D->>D: collect the marked readers
        D->>Rd: rebuild() a build host
        D->>Rd: mark_needs_layout(), invalidate_paint_cache() a leaf
        S->>W: reset the background when it is a token
        S->>W: invalidate()
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The manager has one owner hook.
  • A theme change re-measures as well as repaints.
  • A window background drawn from a token is reset on every theme change.

docs.title: The Lookup
docs.text: Theme.of finds the AppScope above the context and reads the manager's current theme. The parent chain it walks is kept intact by the widgeting layer.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    of[Theme.of]
    find[find_app_scope]
    forget[Widget]
    scope[AppScope]
    mgr[ThemeManager]
    dep[theme/dependency.py]
    build["evaluate_build()"]
    adopt["BuilderHostMixin._adopt_built"]
    store["ChildrenStore.add_child · _detach_parent"]

    of -- "find_app_scope(context)" --> find -- "the nearest AppScope" --> scope
    of -- "scope.theme_manager.current" --> mgr
    forget -- "mount() · unmount(): forget_app_scope(widget)" --> find
    of -- "register_theme_dependency(context)" --> dep
    build -- "push_theme_reader(host) · pop_theme_reader()" --> dep
    adopt -- "built._parent = host, at build" --> find
    store -- "add_child: child._parent = owner · _detach_parent" --> find
Module Role Theme.of resolves the scope, registers the read, falls back to the light default find_app_scope, forget_app_scope walks _parent up to the AppScope, remembers the answer on the context, forgets it at mount and unmount Widget clears the memory at mount and unmount evaluate_build() pushes the build host as the reader around build() BuilderHostMixin._adopt_built links a build result to its host as soon as it is built ChildrenStore links a child to its owner, unlinks it only while the link still points at the owner AppScope, ThemeManager the provider the walk ends at (The Provider) theme/dependency.py the mark and the reader stack (The Dependency)

docs.title: The scope is remembered
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Wd as the widget
    participant T as Theme.of
    participant L as find_app_scope

    Wd->>L: mount() → forget_app_scope
    Wd->>T: the first read
    T->>L: find_app_scope(widget)
    L->>L: walk _parent upward
    alt a scope is found
        L->>Wd: remember it on the widget
        L-->>T: the scope
    else none
        L-->>T: None, nothing remembered
    end
    Wd->>T: a later read
    T->>L: find_app_scope(widget)
    L-->>T: the remembered scope, or a new walk
    Wd->>L: unmount() → forget_app_scope

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A scope the walk found is remembered on the widget until it unmounts. A walk that finds nothing remembers nothing.
  • Every read that resolves a scope marks its reader.
  • A read that resolves no scope returns the light default. It marks nothing.
  • A composable parents its build result when it builds.
  • A ChildrenStore clears a child's _parent only while it still points at the store's owner.

docs.title: The Dependency
docs.text: The dependency module marks a reader, finds the marks when the theme changes, and keeps a resolved value for a leaf painted every frame.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    dep[theme/dependency.py]
    build["evaluate_build()"]
    of[Theme.of]
    scope[AppScope]
    tree[the widget tree]

    build -- "push_theme_reader(host) · pop_theme_reader()" --> dep
    of -- "register_theme_dependency(context)" --> dep
    scope -- "invalidate_theme_readers(root)" --> dep
    dep -- "setattr(reader, _reads_theme, True) · getattr(node, _reads_theme) · rebuild · mark_needs_layout · invalidate_paint_cache" --> tree
    tree -- "ThemeKept.get(context, key, resolve) · theme_generation(context)" --> dep
Module Role theme/dependency.py the reader stack the build hosts stand on; the mark _reads_theme on a reader; the walk over children and built_child that rebuilds the marked hosts and re-measures the marked leaves; theme_generation; ThemeKept evaluate_build() pushes and pops the build host around build() (The Lookup) Theme.of registers each read (The Lookup) AppScope asks for the invalidation on a change (The Provider) the widget tree where the marks sit, what the walk invalidates, and the leaves that keep a value

docs.title: A read inside build() marks the host
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as evaluate_build
    participant H as the build host
    participant T as Theme.of
    participant D as dependency.py

    B->>D: push_theme_reader(host)
    B->>H: build()
    H->>T: Theme.of(self)
    T->>D: register_theme_dependency(self)
    D->>D: the reader is the top of the stack, the host
    D->>H: _reads_theme = True
    T-->>H: the theme
    B->>D: pop_theme_reader()

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The mark lives on the reader, never on the provider.
  • A read inside build() is attributed to the build host. A read outside one is attributed to the context.
  • No widget compares the Theme object. Staleness is the generation.

docs.title: Tray Icon
docs.text: TrayIcon is a model registered on the App, App(window, tray=...). Its menu is the MenuEntry model the menu bar uses (MENU_BAR.md), with the same live sync of label, enabled and checked.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three groups of modules take part, with the menu model, the notification backend and the clock at their edges.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    model[The Model]
    appwin[The App and the Window]
    bridges[The Bridges]
    menus[menus/model.py]
    nsmenu[menus/nsmenu.py]
    notify[platform/notification_win32.py]
    clock[observable/runtime.py]

    appwin -- "_install(app) · _uninstall() · _refresh_dock(visible_windows)" --> model
    model -- "install() · uninstall() · set_dock_visible(visible)" --> bridges
    bridges -- "_activate_item(entry) · _fire_activate(), on the UI thread" --> model
    model -- "MenuEntry" --> menus
    bridges -- "NSMenuBuilder" --> nsmenu
    notify -- "active_bridge().show_balloon(title, body)" --> bridges
    bridges -- "schedule_once(hop, 0)" --> clock
Module Role The Model the icon, the tooltip, the menu, installed, the activation of an entry The App and the Window registers the tray, installs it with the loop, reports window visibility; the window's close button and its hide and show The Bridges show the icon and the menu through AppKit, Win32 or D-Bus menus/model.py MenuEntry, the menu model shared with the menu bar (MENU_BAR.md) menus/nsmenu.py NSMenuBuilder, the NSMenu construction shared with the menu bar (MENU_BAR.md) platform/notification_win32.py the Windows notification backend observable/runtime.py the installed clock (OBSERVABLE.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The tray icon lives as long as the app's loop runs.
  • ExitPolicy is not changed by a tray. It counts the existing windows, hidden ones included.
  • The tray menu renders natively on every platform.
  • A failed install never takes the app down.

docs.title: The Model
docs.text: TrayIcon holds what the bridges show and runs what the bridges report.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    tray[TrayIcon]
    app[App]
    bridge[the platform bridge]
    entry[MenuEntry]
    clock[the installed clock]

    app -- "_install(app) · _uninstall() · _refresh_dock(visible_windows)" --> tray
    tray -- "constructs · install() · uninstall() · set_dock_visible(visible)" --> bridge
    bridge -- "schedule_once(hop, 0)" --> clock -- "_activate_item(entry) · _fire_activate()" --> tray
    tray -- "checked · role · on_select" --> entry
    tray -- "exit() for MenuRole.QUIT" --> app
Module Role TrayIcon holds the icon path, the tooltip, the menu and dock_visibility; picks the bridge per platform; publishes installed; runs an activated entry App installs and removes the tray with the loop, reports the visible-window count (The App and the Window) the platform bridge shows the icon and the menu (The Bridges) MenuEntry an item of the menu (MENU_BAR.md) the installed clock the hop to the UI thread (OBSERVABLE.md)

docs.title: The tray is installed and removed
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as App
    participant T as TrayIcon
    participant B as the platform bridge

    A->>T: _install(app), once the loop is up
    T->>B: construct, install()
    alt install raised
        T->>T: log once, installed stays False
    else installed
        T->>T: installed = True
        T->>B: set_dock_visible(visible_window_count > 0), when dock_visibility is "auto"
    end
    A->>T: _uninstall(), when the loop stops
    T->>T: installed = False
    T->>B: uninstall()

docs.title: An activation reaches the model
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as the platform bridge (its own thread)
    participant C as the installed clock
    participant T as TrayIcon (UI thread)
    participant E as MenuEntry

    B->>C: schedule_once(hop, 0)
    C->>T: _activate_item(entry), or _fire_activate()
    opt entry.checked is an observable
        T->>E: checked = not checked
    end
    alt entry.role is QUIT
        T->>T: app.exit()
    else a window-scoped role
        T->>T: warn once, ignore
    else no role
        T->>E: on_select()
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• installed is True only while a bridge shows the icon.
  • An activation touches the model on the UI thread only.
  • A tray menu does not render shortcut.

docs.title: The App and the Window
docs.text: The app registers the tray and installs it with the loop. The window's close button, its hide and its show are what a resident app is built from.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    runner[backends/pyglet/runner.py]
    app[runtime/app.py]
    window[runtime/window.py]
    tray[platform/tray.py]

    runner -- "_install_tray() · _uninstall_tray()" --> app
    app -- "_install(app) · _uninstall() · _refresh_dock(visible_windows)" --> tray
    window -- "_window_visibility_changed() on show · hide · open · close" --> app
    window -- "installed.value, before hiding the last visible window" --> tray
Module Role backends/pyglet/runner.py calls the install once the loop is up and the uninstall when it stops runtime/app.py App holds the registered tray, counts the visible windows, applies the exit policy to the open windows runtime/window.py Window.close_action decides what the OS close button does; hide() and show() toggle visibility; is_visible reports it platform/tray.py the registered model (The Model)

docs.title: The close button hides into the tray
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant OS as the OS close button
    participant W as Window
    participant A as App
    participant T as TrayIcon

    OS->>W: _handle_close_request()
    W->>W: read close_action
    alt "close"
        W->>W: close()
    else "hide"
        opt no other window is visible, and no tray is showing
            W->>W: warn once
        end
        W->>W: hide(): is_visible = False, set_visible(False)
        W->>A: _window_visibility_changed()
        A->>T: _refresh_dock(visible_window_count)
        opt dock_visibility is "auto"
            T->>T: bridge.set_dock_visible(visible_window_count > 0)
        end
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• close_action remaps the OS close button only. close() and the menu roles always close.
  • A hidden window keeps its tree, its state and its geometry. It renders no frames.
  • A hide() before the backend realises the OS window creates it invisible.
  • dock_visibility="auto" keeps the Dock icon while a window is visible and drops it when none is.

docs.title: The Bridges
docs.text: One bridge per platform shows the icon and the menu.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    tray[platform/tray.py]
    cocoa[platform/tray_cocoa.py]
    win32[platform/tray_win32.py]
    sni[platform/tray_sni.py]
    nsmenu[menus/nsmenu.py]
    win32plan[platform/tray_win32_plan.py]
    sniplan[platform/tray_sni_plan.py]
    appkit["AppKit, through pyglet's cocoapy"]
    shell["Win32, through ctypes"]
    dbus["the session bus, through jeepney"]
    notify[platform/notification_win32.py]
    clock[observable/runtime.py]

    tray -- "install() · uninstall() · set_dock_visible(visible)" --> cocoa & win32 & sni
    cocoa -- "NSMenuBuilder.new_menu(entries)" --> nsmenu
    cocoa -- "statusItemWithLength_ · setActivationPolicy_" --> appkit
    win32 -- "plan_menu(entries) · load_icon_bgra(path, size)" --> win32plan
    win32 -- "RegisterClassW · CreateWindowExW · Shell_NotifyIconW · TrackPopupMenu" --> shell
    sni -- "plan_menu(entries) · load_icon_argb(path)" --> sniplan
    sni -- "RegisterStatusNotifierItem · GetLayout · LayoutUpdated · Event" --> dbus
    notify -- "show_balloon(title, body)" --> win32
    cocoa & win32 & sni -- "schedule_once(hop, 0)" --> clock
Module Role platform/tray.py the model the bridges show (The Model) platform/tray_cocoa.py an NSStatusItem with the menu NSMenuBuilder builds; switches the activation policy for the Dock platform/tray_win32.py a dedicated thread owning a hidden top-level window and its message loop; the icon through Shell_NotifyIcon; the menu built per right click; the balloon platform/tray_sni.py a StatusNotifierItem and its dbusmenu on the session bus; a receiver thread serving the desktop's calls; registers again when the watcher's bus name changes owner menus/nsmenu.py NSMenuBuilder, shared with the menu bar (MENU_BAR.md) platform/tray_win32_plan.py flattens the menu into Win32 items and command ids; decodes the icon with skia platform/tray_sni_plan.py flattens the menu into a dbusmenu layout and item ids; decodes the icon with skia AppKit the status bar and the application's activation policy Win32 the notification area and the popup menu the session bus the desktop's StatusNotifierWatcher, which draws the icon and the menu platform/notification_win32.py the Windows notification backend observable/runtime.py the installed clock (OBSERVABLE.md)

docs.title: The desktop asks for the menu again
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant T as TrayIcon
    participant S as tray_sni.py
    participant D as the session bus

    T->>S: a label, enabled or checked changed, through its subscription
    S->>S: revision += 1
    S->>D: LayoutUpdated(revision, root)
    D->>S: GetLayout
    S->>S: plan_menu(entries), afresh
    S-->>D: the layout, ids in tree order
    D->>S: Event(id, "clicked")
    S->>T: hop: _activate_item(entry)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A bridge keeps no menu state between the desktop's requests. The model is the only copy.
  • While a tray is installed, a Windows notification balloon hangs on its icon. Without one the notification backend adds a transient icon of its own.
  • Windows and Linux decode the icon with skia. macOS hands the file to AppKit.

docs.title: Typography
docs.text: A Text draws a string. Its metrics come from a TypeScaleToken, its layout from the widget itself, its look from a TextStyle.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Four groups of modules take part, with the Material components and the app at their edges.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    token[The Token]
    text[The Text]
    tstyle[The Style]
    font[The Font Path]
    material[the Material components]
    app[the app]

    app -- "Text(label, type_scale, style, alignment, max_lines, ...)" --> text
    material -- "TypeScale.ROLE · TypeScaleToken.from_size(size)" --> token
    material -- "TextStyle(color, font_family)" --> tstyle
    text -- "font_size · line_height · weight · tracking" --> token
    text -- "color · font_family" --> tstyle
    text -- "get_typeface · measure_text_width · measure_text_ink_bounds · make_text_blob" --> font
Module Role The Token the metrics of one MD3 type-scale role The Text the widget The Style the colour and the font family The Font Path the typeface, the measurements and the shaped text the Material components own their typography (MATERIAL_INTERACTION.md) the app constructs a Text

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• An MD3 type-scale metric is on the token. A property of the layout inside the box is on Text. A reusable visual property is on TextStyle.
  • No merged object stands between the token and the style. A token is never expanded into a TextStyle.

docs.title: The Token
docs.text: A role's metrics travel together as one TypeScaleToken.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    token[theme/type_scale.py]
    text[widgets/text.py]
    material[the Material components]
    app[the app]

    text -- "font_size · line_height · weight · tracking · DEFAULT_TYPE_SCALE" --> token
    material -- "TypeScale.HEADLINE_SMALL · BODY_MEDIUM · LABEL_MEDIUM · LABEL_LARGE · from_size(style.font_size)" --> token
    app -- "TypeScale.ROLE · ROLE.copy_with(weight)" --> token
Module Role theme/type_scale.py TypeScaleToken, a frozen struct of font size, line height, weight and tracking; TypeScale, the MD3 baseline roles; the default role widgets/text.py reads the metrics (The Text) the Material components pick the role MD3 fixes, or wrap a style's numeric size the app picks a role

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• A size from a widget's *Style becomes a full token through from_size.
  • Where MD3 fixes a component's role, the component uses that role.

docs.title: The Text
docs.text: TextBase lays its string out inside its box.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    text[widgets/text.py]
    mtext[material/text.py]
    token[theme/type_scale.py]
    tstyle[widgets/text_style.py]
    font[rendering/skia/font.py]
    theme[theme/theme.py]

    mtext -- "is a" --> text
    text -- "type_scale, or DEFAULT_TYPE_SCALE" --> token
    text -- "style.color · style.font_family" --> tstyle
    mtext -- "Theme.of(self), the Material TextStyle" --> theme
    text -- "get_typeface(family, weight) · measure_text_width(tf, size, text, tracking) · measure_text_ink_bounds(...) · make_text_blob(line, font, tracking)" --> font
Module Role widgets/text.py TextBase: the alignment, the wrapping, max_lines, the overflow, the truncation; the runs and the paint cache material/text.py Text, defaulting its style to the current Material theme's theme/type_scale.py the metrics (The Token) widgets/text_style.py the look (The Style) rendering/skia/font.py the typeface, the measurements and the blob (The Font Path) theme/theme.py the Material default style (THEME_CONSUMPTION.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Font size, weight and tracking reach the Skia font path. Line height places the lines.
  • Wrapping and ellipsis are measured with the same tracking the blob is shaped with.

docs.title: The Style
docs.text: TextStyle is the colour and the font family.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    core[widgets/text_style.py]
    mstyle[material/styles/text_style.py]
    text[widgets/text.py]
    material[the Material components]
    role[material/theme/color_role.py]

    text -- "TextStyleProtocol: color · font_family" --> core
    mstyle -- "satisfies TextStyleProtocol" --> core
    mstyle -- "ColorRole.ON_SURFACE, the default colour" --> role
    material -- "*Style.text_color · *Style.font_family" --> mstyle
Module Role widgets/text_style.py TextStyle; TextStyleProtocol, what a Text reads material/styles/text_style.py the Material TextStyle widgets/text.py reads the protocol (The Text) the Material components expose the visual overrides on their *Style material/theme/color_role.py the colour roles (STYLE_THEME.md)

docs.title: Promises
docs.text: • A TextStyle carries color and font_family. Nothing else.

docs.title: Web Target
docs.text: One app runs on the desktop and in a browser from the same source. In the browser, Pyodide runs the app's Python unmodified. A CanvasKit adapter with the shape of skia-python draws it onto one canvas. The browser's event loop replaces the pyglet one. The two marks an app makes for the web, @worker and @server, run on the desktop too.

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• The rendering code is the desktop code.
  • The adapter covers the calls the framework makes.
  • The canvas matrix lives in Python. It reaches CanvasKit once per run of draws.
  • Geometry and paint state cross to JS as plain numbers, once per draw.
  • Every font family name resolves to the typefaces the page loaded.
  • A frame runs only when one was asked for.
  • The WebGL surface is made again when the canvas or the device pixel ratio changes. That frame repaints everything.
  • A deadline within a frame's time waits for the next frame. A later one is a setTimeout.
  • The main window fills the canvas.
  • From the host boundary on, the key handling is the desktop's.
  • The clipboard crosses in one direction at a time. A copy writes through navigator.clipboard. A paste arrives only as a paste event.

docs.title: A worker call
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as the app (UI thread)
    participant F as remote/function.py
    participant Wf as remote/worker.py
    participant P as remote/pool.py
    participant T as the transport (threads.py, process.py or workers.mjs)
    participant Wr as remote/writer.py
    participant O as the caller's Observable

    App->>F: await fn(args, progress)
    F->>F: encode the arguments by their codecs
    F->>Wf: _call_on_web, or _call_on_desktop
    Wf->>P: call(name, ceiling, values, writers)
    P->>P: queue, then run when fewer calls of fn run than its ceiling and a worker is idle or can start
    P->>T: start(slot) if needed, post(call_id, name, values)
    loop while the function runs
        T-->>P: a message per write to a progress parameter
        P->>Wr: CallWriter.receive(value)
        Wr->>O: the latest value per clock tick
    end
    alt the function returns
        T-->>P: the result, or the error
        P-->>Wf: the encoded result
        Wf-->>F: the encoded result
        F-->>App: decoded, or a builtin exception by type, or RemoteError
    else the caller cancels
        App--xP: CancelledError
        alt the call is queued
            P->>P: forget it
        else the call is running
            P->>T: end(), and another starts when a call needs it
        end
    end

docs.title: Promises
docs.text:
• Both marks go on a module-level function. The app calls it the same way on both targets, await fn(...).
  • On the desktop a call of either mark runs on a thread the runtime owns, or in a child process under process.
  • The arguments, the result and every progress write pass through the codec on both targets.
  • The codec comes from the type annotations, never from the data. A type the codec has no rule for is refused when the function is defined.
  • Progress flows through a WriteOnlyObservable parameter. The caller's observable takes the latest value per clock tick.
  • The CancelToken is a parameter with a default. On a thread, cancelling sets it. In a worker or a child process, cancelling ends the Python running the call.
  • A builtin exception raised in the function is raised again in the caller by type. Any other arrives as RemoteError.
  • @worker marks a function in a module the browser gets.
  • The ceiling is per function. The pool is per kind, grown to the largest ceiling and never past the machine's cores.
  • A worker that ends on its own fails its call with ConnectionError. One that never becomes ready fails every call until the pool is retired.
  • A child process imports the functions' modules by name. It imports the entry script the way multiprocessing does.
  • Hot reload retires the desktop's pools.

docs.title: Nuiitivet Guides
docs.text: This section is the practical user guide for building apps with Nuiitivet. Use it as a step-by-step path from fundamentals to common app patterns.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
Nuiitivet has a single import root: your chosen UI design system. Import it once as nv, and every symbol — layout, state, widgets, styles, modifiers — is reachable from there.

import nuiitivet.material as nv

nv.Column([nv.Text("Hello"), nv.Button("Click")])

An app always uses exactly one design system, so selecting it should hand you the whole toolkit in one import. Only nuiitivet.material is available today.

docs.title: Concurrency: choosing a tool
docs.text:
Work that takes time — a search, a file read, a long import — must not run on the UI thread, or the window stops painting until it finishes. Its result must not reach a widget from the thread that produced it either.

Both halves already have answers, and none of them involve writing marshalling code by hand. Find your situation below.

docs.title: Which tool
docs.text: Your situation Reach for Read A value derived from another, asynchronously — the map whose transform takes time. A SearchBar that searches as you type switch_map Async State I/O in an event handler, and the screen just waits for it an async handler, awaiting the call — no thread involved Heavy work in an event handler, and the screen just waits for it an async handler, await asyncio.to_thread(...) — a thread, but the runtime owns it Thread Safety The same heavy work, but it should report progress and be cancellable a hand-written worker thread Background Work A thread in an app that also runs in a browser a @nv.worker function; @nv.server when the work needs a server Worker and Server Functions The same, but no more than N calls at a time @nv.worker(parallel=N) Worker and Server Functions Work that needs a process: pure Python that should use another core, a loop that never checks its token, native code that may crash @nv.worker(process=True) Worker and Server Functions Values arriving faster than the screen needs them debounce() / throttle() Practical Controls Getting a worker's result onto the UI thread nothing — an observable write is marshalled for you Thread Safety A consumer that must see every intermediate value, not the newest dispatch=False Thread Safety Testing an async handler await app.idle(), await app.wait_for(...) Testing async flows Testing a write that came from a worker thread app.settle() Thread Safety

docs.title: Geometry: scoped measured size
docs.text:
Most adaptive layout is a widget reacting to its own box, which on_size_changed handles with one modifier. Reach for Geometry for the other shape of the problem: one measured box, many readers — widgets nested at arbitrary depth that must react to an ancestor's size, without every widget in between having to pass it through.

Geometry wraps a single child and is transparent to layout: the child receives the same size Geometry receives. After each layout pass it publishes its own resolved size as an Observable[Size], which descendants read with Geometry.of(self).size.

Two rules come with it, and they are the reason this is the advanced tool:

  • Bind the Observable; never read .value at build time. .value is a one-time snapshot that never updates. Map it into a value widget, or drive a Deck index for a structural switch.
  • Resolve it in on_mount, not __init__. Geometry.of walks the ancestor chain, and a widget has no ancestors until it is mounted. build() then just references what on_mount derived. Get this wrong and the error says so — a premature of() reports that the widget was not mounted yet, rather than blaming a missing Geometry provider.

docs.title: One box, many readers
docs.text:
import nuiitivet.material as nv

_WIDE = 600


class SizeClassBadge(nv.ComposableWidget):
    """A leaf, nested arbitrarily deep, that reads the pane it lives in."""

    def on_mount(self) -> None:
        size = nv.Geometry.of(self).size
        self._label = size.map(lambda s: f"{'expanded' if s.width >= _WIDE else 'compact'} · {s.width}px")
        super().on_mount()

    def build(self) -> nv.Widget:
        return nv.Text(self._label, width=150)


class _Section(nv.ComposableWidget):
    """An intermediate widget: it holds a badge but knows nothing about size."""

    def __init__(self, title: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(width="wt")
        self._title = title

    def build(self) -> nv.Widget:
        return nv.Card(
            nv.Row([nv.Text(self._title), nv.Spacer(width="wt"), SizeClassBadge()],
                   gap=12, padding=16, width="wt", cross_alignment="center"),
            width="wt",
        )


# One filling Geometry defines the scope for every badge below it.
nv.Geometry(
    nv.Column([_Section("Library"), _Section("Downloads"), _Section("Settings")],
              gap=16, width="wt", height="wt"),
    width="wt",
    height="wt",
)

_Section passes nothing down — it does not know that a badge somewhere inside it cares about the pane's width. Move the badge elsewhere and it reads whatever pane it lands in.

docs.title: Two kinds of binding
docs.text:
• Read-only (a label, a Deck index): map straight from size — e.g. Text(size.map(...)), Deck(index=size.map(...)). Deck accepts a derived .map(...) index and shows one mounted child by it.
  • Two-way widget state (a NavigationRail's expanded, which its own menu button can also toggle): a read-only .map cannot be written back, so mirror the size-derived value into a plain Observable and keep it in sync — and at that point on_size_changed is usually the simpler tool.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Nearest provider wins. Geometry.of(self) resolves to the nearest ancestor Geometry, so a nested one overrides the window for its subtree. The app installs a root Geometry provider at the window, so with no nearer provider a read falls back to it and tracks the window size.
  • A filling Geometry measures available space. width="wt" makes it fill what the parent offers, so it measures the space available to a pane rather than the child's intrinsic size.
  • The size lands on the next frame. It is measured during layout and published between frames, so every consumer — a mapped label or a Deck switching arrangements — sees it on the following frame. Imperceptible, and it keeps the layout pass free of subtree rebuilds.
  • Stable sizes don't re-fire. An unchanged size is de-duped, so a Geometry whose size is imposed by its parent cannot drive a feedback loop.
  • Size is a (width, height) pair: size.width, size.height, or unpack it with w, h = size.

docs.title: Choosing between the two
docs.text: Use for on_size_changed Push, to itself. This component reacts to its own box. No lifecycle override, no subscription, no scope. Geometry Pull, from a scope. Many widgets, at any depth, read one ancestor's box.

docs.title: InteractionRegion / InteractionState (Advanced)
docs.text: ⚠️ This document targets advanced users who need to integrate deeply with the interaction system. Regular Modifier chaining (hoverable(), clickable()) already covers the common cases without exposing these types.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
nuiitivet.widgets.interaction.InteractionRegion is the thin wrapper that powers pointer-related Modifiers. Whenever you chain hoverable() or clickable() the modifier ensures that the target Widget is wrapped in a single InteractionRegion instance. Multiple pointer modifiers automatically reuse the same wrapper, so order does not matter.

┌──────────────┐   hoverable()   clickable()
│   Widget     │ ─────────────▶ InteractionRegion (shared)
└──────────────┘

The region hosts an InteractionState object that records the live pointer flags:

Field Meaning hovered Pointer is inside the region (or captured and still over the rect). pressed Active press sequence is in progress. focused Widget is focused (set by App-level focus handling). disabled Modifier or widget marked the interaction as disabled. dragging / scrolling Reserved for drag/scroll modifiers. selected, checked, toggled_on Convenience flags for composite controls. pointer_position Latest pointer coordinate while hovering. press_position Coordinate of the press that started the current gesture.

The same state object is injected into the wrapped child, so advanced widgets can read or mutate it directly if needed (e.g., a custom control syncing state.disabled with its own model).

docs.title: Programmatic Access
docs.text:
from nuiitivet.widgets.interaction import InteractionRegion, InteractionState

state = InteractionState(disabled=False)
region = InteractionRegion(custom_child, state=state)
region.enable_hover()
region.enable_click(on_click=lambda: print("clicked"))

docs.title: InteractionController
docs.text:
InteractionRegion internally uses InteractionController to translate pointer events into InteractionState updates. You usually do not need to touch it, but advanced widgets (such as BaseButton) can embed the controller directly to keep their concrete class (and public API) intact:

import nuiitivet.material as nv
from nuiitivet.widgets.interaction import InteractionController, InteractionState

class FancyControl(nv.Widget):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.interaction_state = InteractionState()
        self._interaction = InteractionController(self, self.interaction_state)
        self._interaction.enable_hover()
        self._interaction.enable_click(on_click=self._on_activate)

    def on_pointer_event(self, event: nv.PointerEvent) -> bool:
        return self._interaction.handle_pointer_event(event, self.global_visual_rect)

Using the controller directly keeps the widget class (and its attributes) visible to the outside world, while still benefiting from the shared pointer logic.

docs.title: Practical Guidelines
docs.text:
1. Do not expose InteractionRegion in beginner-facing docs or APIs. End users should only see Modifier.hoverable() / Modifier.clickable().
  2. Limit manual usage to custom containers that need to intercept pointer events before decoration or layout occurs.
  3. State-first design. Widgets should read interaction_state when computing overlays, focus rings, etc., so modifiers and direct integrations stay in sync.
  4. Release-triggered clicks. The controller follows standard UI semantics: press captures the pointer, release inside the rect fires the click. Make sure your tests reflect this order.
  5. No shim layers. If you need bespoke behavior (e.g., drag handles), implement a dedicated modifier or controller hook instead of stacking ad-hoc event handlers.

docs.title: With a coding agent
docs.text:
Once a coding agent has the first version of an app on screen, the rest is refining what works and fixing what behaves wrong, and both are hard to put into chat. These pages move that work onto the running app itself. They assume you already work with a coding agent such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot.

If you want to… Read Get the dev extra, the skills and the MCP server in place, and your app running under the dev runner Set up See every save rebuild the running window, with state and breakpoints intact Hot Reload Tell the agent what to change, or what went wrong, from the app's own screen Comment mode Fix a size, an order, a spacing or a style yourself, on the screen Layout edit mode Read or edit the code behind a widget Source jump Know what each skill does for you The skills Let the agent see, drive and check the running app, or drive it yourself from a terminal The dev bridge

docs.title: Comment mode
docs.text: Telling an agent where is often the hard part of telling it what to do. Comment mode puts the instruction on the app itself.

docs.title: 1. Have the agent answer your comments
docs.text: The agent answers on the marks either way. A watch answers every Send of the session; a read answers what you have sent so far.

docs.title: Watch for every Send
docs.text: In chat, once per session: /nuiitivet-see-comments watch. From then on the agent answers each Send you make in the app; no chat message is needed.

docs.title: Read once
docs.text: /nuiitivet-see-comments in chat reads and answers what you have sent, once. Without the skill installed, see_comments does the same.

docs.title: 2. Enter the mode
docs.text: Press Ctrl+Shift+C (Cmd+Shift+C on macOS). The mode's name and H help show at the centre for a moment.

docs.title: 3. Mark the place
docs.text: Hover, and the widget under the cursor gets amber corner brackets and a caption naming it: the one a click would mark. Click, and a numbered badge sits at its corner from then on.

docs.title: Mark an empty area
docs.text: Drag instead of clicking to mark an area — a gap, a misaligned band, anywhere with no widget to name.

docs.title: Aim at a covered or tiny widget
docs.text: When the widget you mean is covered by its children or too small to aim at, walk to it from the keys. W / S move the choice up to its parent and back down. A / D move it along to the widget beside it. Enter or a click then marks it.

docs.title: 4. Write the instruction
docs.text: A field opens on the mark. Type what you want done and press Enter.

docs.title: Leave the mark bare and name it in chat
docs.text: A mark with no text is fine. Name it by its number in chat.

docs.title: Report a problem instead of a change
docs.text: Write what went wrong, right after it happens. The agent reads the clicks and keys you made just before, and reproduces the problem before fixing it.

docs.title: Change or clear what you wrote
docs.text: Before the agent answers, click the marked widget or its badge: the field opens again on your text. Enter with the text emptied keeps just the number. Esc closes the field without a change. On a mark you just made with nothing written yet, Esc removes the mark too.

docs.title: 5. Send to the agent
docs.text: Mark as many places as you like, then press Ctrl+Enter, or the Send button at the window's bottom-right. The button hides below the window's edge with a sliver showing. Bring the pointer to the sliver and it stands up. What goes out is the mark and your words on it. Nothing you type elsewhere in the app ever does.

docs.title: 6. Read the answer
docs.text: After a Send, a grey disc with an hourglass joins the number of every mark the agent has not answered yet. Stay in the mode: the hourglass turns into a coloured disc, green with a check mark for done, red with a cross for refused, blue with a question mark for a question to you. Hover the badge to read the thread under it: your lines and the agent's, each led by an icon for who wrote it. A thread taller than the window shows its newest lines and counts the rest.

docs.title: 7. Act on the answer
docs.text: A question, or a refused you disagree with, gets a reply. A done, or a refusal you accept, gets removed.

docs.title: Reply on a mark
docs.text: Click the mark: the field opens empty for your reply. Write and send as before. The agent reads the whole thread.

docs.title: Remove a mark
docs.text: Delete or Backspace removes the mark under the cursor, on its widget or on its badge. Ctrl+Backspace removes every mark, sent ones included. Ctrl+Z brings them back.

docs.title: 8. Leave
docs.text: Press Esc when you want the app back. The marks go off the screen but stay, sent or not, and come back with the mode. The line at the centre says unsent comments if you left something the agent has not seen.

docs.title: Every gesture
docs.text: Gesture What it does Ctrl+Shift+C Enter comment mode (Cmd+Shift+C on macOS — either accelerator works throughout). Hold H Show every gesture of this mode while the key is down. Hover The widget under the cursor gets amber corner brackets and a caption naming it: the one a click would mark. W / S, A / D Move that choice up to its parent and back down, or along to the widget beside it. Enter or a click then marks it. Click Mark the widget under the cursor; a field opens on the mark. On a marked widget, or on its numbered badge, the field opens again instead: on your text, to change or clear it, or empty once the agent has answered, to reply. Drag Mark an area instead. The field opens the same way. In the field Enter keeps the text (empty keeps just the number); Ctrl+Enter keeps it and sends; Shift+Enter breaks the line; Esc closes the field, and removes a new mark with nothing written (Ctrl+Z brings it back). Shift+←/→ selects, Ctrl+A/C/X/V (Cmd on macOS) select all, copy, cut and paste. A click keeps the text and then does what it would have done anyway. Ctrl+Enter, or Send, the button at the bottom-right Send your comments to the agent. The button stands up when the pointer reaches its sliver at the window's edge. A click there also keeps the open field. The badge After Send, a grey disc with an hourglass until the agent answers; then green with a check mark for done, red with a cross for refused, blue with a question mark for a question to you. Hover a mark's numbered badge Read its thread under the badge, each line led by an icon for who wrote it; a thread taller than the window shows its newest lines and counts the rest. Delete / Backspace Remove the mark under the cursor, on its widget or on its badge. Ctrl+Z brings it back. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z Undo and redo what you did since you last sent — a mark, an unmark, a text. The same keys as layout edit mode. Ctrl+Backspace Remove every mark, sent ones included. Ctrl+Z brings them back. Esc Leave. The marks go off the screen but stay, sent or not; enter again and they are back as you left them. Ctrl+Shift+E Switch to layout edit mode, your marks kept.
